Currently, I need to design a management and approval mechanism. Extensions are categorized into Official and Unofficial. When a user uploads an extension, it is designated as Unofficial by default. Elevating an extension to "Official" status requires an approval process.

There are two tiers of official status: Product-Line Level and Company Level. Approval administrators are designated based on the functional category for each tier. Users will select their target tier (Product-Line Level or Company Level) and category for their application, which will then be reviewed by the specific administrator assigned to that combination. The administrator matrix must be fully configurable.

1	# AgentCenter (Nuxt) — Implementation Plan
2	
3	Marketplace for AI agent extensions (Skills, MCP servers, slash commands, plugins) with internal-enterprise features (departments, scope, tags, collections) and a companion CLI for actual machine-side install.
4	
5	This is a Nuxt 4 rewrite of the original Next.js implementation at `../agentcenter/`. The product surface and the public `/api/v1` contract are preserved verbatim so the existing CLI keeps working unchanged.
6	
7	This document is the living plan. When a binding decision changes, update it in the same commit as the code change.

10	
11	## 1. Project layout
12	
13	File-based routing under `app/pages/`, Nitro server under `server/`, and a cross-cutting `shared/` directory that both sides import from. Single Nuxt app, server-side rendering by default. The CLI is a sibling directory (`cli/`) carried over verbatim from the original repo.
14	
15	**Locale prefixing**: `@nuxtjs/i18n` with `strategy: "prefix"` auto-prefixes every page route with `/en` and `/zh` — pages live at `app/pages/index.vue`, **not** `app/pages/[locale]/index.vue`. URLs are always prefixed (`/en/...`, `/zh/...`); the locale segment is owned by the i18n module, not the file system. This is a structural difference from the original Next.js layout, which used an explicit `[locale]` directory segment.

186	
187	**API routes vs server actions**: Nuxt has no server actions. The Next.js implementation used server actions for user-initiated mutations from RSC pages (install toggle from web, save-to-collection, create collection, draft create/update). All of these become POST handlers under `server/api/internal/...` called via `$fetch` from client components. Validation lives in the handler using the same Zod schemas as before; the handler is the new trust boundary. API routes under `/api/v1/...` (public, CLI-consumed), `/api/auth/...` (Better Auth), `/api/upload/sign` (presigned URL), and `/api/inngest` (webhook) keep their original purpose.

212	
213	## 3. Drizzle schema
214	
215	**The schema is portable verbatim from `../agentcenter/lib/db/schema/`.** Same tables, same columns, same indexes, same enums. The `drizzle/` migrations directory is copied across as-is. See the original `docs/plan.md` §3 for the full table specification — it is the source of truth for column types and indexes, and is not re-pasted here to avoid drift.
216	
217	Driver change: the original used `@neondatabase/serverless` (HTTP). We use `drizzle-orm/postgres-js` (TCP) with a standard `DATABASE_URL`. This works against Supabase, self-hosted Postgres, or any vanilla Postgres. No code change in queries.
218	
219	```ts
220	// server/utils/db.ts
221	import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/postgres-js"
222	import postgres from "postgres"
223	import * as schema from "~~/shared/db/schema"
224	
225	const client = postgres(process.env.DATABASE_URL!, { prepare: false })
226	export const db = drizzle(client, { schema })
227	```
228	
229	Critical indexing notes — unchanged from the original:
230	
231	- Department descendant matching uses the dotted-path id directly: `WHERE deptId = $1 OR deptId LIKE $1 || '.%'`. This requires `text_pattern_ops` on `deptId` to use the index for `LIKE`. No recursive CTE.
232	- `(funcCat, subCat, l2)` covers drill-down.
233	- Sort indexes are separate (`downloadsCount DESC`, `starsAvg DESC`).
234

236	
237	## 4. i18n strategy
238	
239	- **Module**: `@nuxtjs/i18n` with `strategy: 'prefix'`. Locales `en` (default) | `zh`. **Always-prefixed URLs** (`/en/...`, `/zh/...`). A global middleware (`app/middleware/locale-redirect.global.ts`) redirects bare `/` → `/en` based on `Accept-Language`.
240	- **Static UI strings**: `i18n/locales/{en,zh}.json`, namespaced by feature (`Sidebar.browse`, `FilterBar.scope.personal`, `Card.installed`). Reuse the prototype's `T` keys verbatim. Use the `$t()` / `t()` helpers from `useI18n()` in components.
241	- **Dynamic content** (extension names, descriptions, dept names, tag labels, changelogs): **column-per-language** (`name` + `nameZh`, `description` + `descriptionZh`). Locked decision; same rationale as the original.
242	- **Tag labels**: `tags` table carries `labelEn` + `labelZh`. The `useTagLabel(tag)` composable picks the right column from `useI18n().locale`.
243	- **Locale switcher**: `<NuxtLink>` swapping the locale segment via `switchLocalePath()`; preserves filter query string.
244	- **FTS**: separate weighted tsvector concatenating all language variants — see §8.
245

249	
250	Three themes shipped: **Editorial Ivory** (default), **Dark**, and **Mono Clean**.
251	
252	Theme tokens in `app/assets/css/tailwind.css` via Tailwind v4 `@theme` blocks. Ivory lives in the base `@theme` block; Dark and Mono Clean live behind `.dark` and `.mono` class selectors applied to `<html>`:

297	
298	`ThemeSwitch` is a dropdown (sun / moon / contrast icons + preview tiles per option) that writes the `theme` cookie. `useTheme` reads the cookie via `useCookie` and applies the matching class (`""` for ivory, `dark`, `mono`) to `<html>` via `useHead` — serialised into the SSR HTML so the initial paint already carries the correct theme, no flash on hydrate. Fonts loaded via `@nuxt/fonts` and wired into the CSS variables.
299	
300	### Accent usage convention
301	
302	`--color-accent` is the only chromatic token in the editorial palette, so it has to be spent carefully. Locked decision #11 (in `CLAUDE.md`) governs where it appears.
303	
304	**Use accent for:**
305	- Primary CTAs (Install on the detail page, the home hero's "View extension" arrow).
306	- Focus rings on form inputs and interactive controls.
307	- The home featured hero (left-rule + CTA arrow only).
308	- The Extension detail page's install button.
309	
310	**Do NOT use accent for:**
311	- Sidebar active state — use a 2px left rule in `--color-ink`, plus `bg-(--color-sidebar)/60` and `font-semibold`. No tinted fills, no accent on the rule itself.
312	- Filter trigger pills (Dept, FuncCategory, Creator, Publisher, TagDrawer) when applied — use `border-(--color-ink)/35 + font-semibold` instead of tinted fill.
313	- Inner popover chips and row selections — neutral ink + `font-semibold`. The popover is itself a focused interaction; the selected row reads as "current" through weight without needing chromatic emphasis.
314	- Decorative dots and bullets in the sidebar — use `bg-(--color-ink-muted)`.
315	
316	**Exempt (intentionally accent-heavy):**
317	- Auth flows (sign-in, sign-up, CLI device auth, onboarding) — these screens are essentially landing pages with one CTA each.
318	- UI primitive focus rings (`Button`, `Input`, `Checkbox`, `SelectTrigger`, `Textarea`) — accent focus is a system signal, not chrome.
319	- Error boundaries — the retry CTA carries the accent fill.
320	
321	Rule of thumb: a viewport should carry **at most two** intentional accent moments. The home should typically have **one** (the featured hero or the fallback CTA). When introducing a new accent hit, ask whether it's earning attention or just adding noise — if removing it doesn't degrade comprehension, remove it.
322

324	
325	## 6. Auth & access model
326	
327	**Better Auth.** Cookie-based server-side sessions; no JWTs. Drizzle adapter; auth tables live in `shared/db/schema/auth.ts`. Same shape as the original — no schema change.
328	
329	- **Sign-up policy**: open. Email + password for v1; SSO/SAML deferred.
330	- **MVP roles** (on `memberships.role`): `viewer`, `publisher`, `admin`.
331	- **Onboarding step** at `/[locale]/onboard` after first sign-up. Enforced by `require-onboard` middleware on the home, browse, and publish routes.
332	- **CLI auth**: device-code OAuth flow on top of Better Auth's `verifications` table — identical scheme to the original.
333	  1. `POST /api/v1/auth/device/code` → creates two `verifications` rows (`dc:poll:<deviceCode>` and `dc:user:<userCode>`) and returns the user code.
334	  2. User opens `/[locale]/cli/auth`, signs in, enters the user code; the page resolves user code → device code, marks the poll row authorized, and stores a session token in it.
335	  3. CLI polls `POST /api/v1/auth/device/poll` every 5s. When authorized, the token is returned once and the row is deleted.
336	  4. Token stored at `~/.config/agentcenter/credentials.json` (mode 0600).
337	
338	The Better Auth client lives in `useAuth()` composable; the server-side helper `requireUser(event)` lives in `server/utils/auth.ts` and is the single place that decides whether an incoming request has a valid session (cookie *or* Bearer header — same `sessions` table backs both).
339

342	## 7. Upload pipeline
343	
344	The wizard is a 4-step rail layout (`<UploadWizard>` in `app/components/publish/`): **Basics → Bundle → Listing → Review**, with a sticky live-preview pane that mirrors the listing card and the derived `manifest.json`. Step 1 (Basics) creates the draft on advance; Steps 2-3 mutate it; Step 4 submits.
345	
346	```text
347	Browser                          Nitro                          Storage      Inngest
348	   │ Basics → Next                  │                              │             │
349	   ├──── POST /api/internal/publish/create-draft ───►│  extensions row (visibility=draft)
350	   │                                │                              │             │
351	   ├──── Bundle: upload .zip ───────│─── presigned PUT URL ───────►│             │
352	   │                                │                              │             │
353	   ├──── POST /api/internal/publish/attach-file ────►│  files row + extensionVersion
354	   │                                │                              │             │
355	   ├──── Listing/Review edits ─────► /api/internal/publish/update-draft
356	   │                                │                              │             │
357	   ├──── Review → Publish ─────────► /api/internal/publish/submit ──► sendEvent("extension/scan.requested")
358	   │                                │                              │             │
359	   │                                │                              │  scan-bundle:
360	   │                                │                              │   download from storage,
361	   │                                │                              │   sha-256 checksum,
362	   │                                │                              │   parse manifest.toml,
363	   │                                │                              │   validate schema,
364	   │                                │                              │   recordScanResult →
365	   │                                │                              │    scope=personal → auto-publish
366	   │                                │                              │    scope=org|enterprise → await admin
367	   │                                │                              │   sendEvent("extension/index.requested")
368	   │                                │                              │             │
369	   │                                │                              │  reindex-search:
370	   │                                │                              │   bust route cache for browse pages
371	```
372	
373	**Synchronous** (server endpoint, returns < 200ms): manifest creation, presigned URL signing, attach-file, submit.
374	**Async** (Inngest): bundle download, scan, validation, indexing, publish flip.
375	
376	Implementation notes — unchanged from the original:
377	
378	- Bundle keys: `bundles/<slug>/<version>/bundle.zip` (`bundleKey()` in `server/utils/storage.ts`). `slug` and `version` are locked on the Basics step once a draft has been persisted.
379	- `submit(versionId)` is idempotent for `pending|scanning` so retries don't get stuck.
380	- `recordScanResult` branches on `extensions.scope`: `personal` auto-publishes; `org|enterprise` waits for admin `publishVersion`.
381	- `extensions.search_vector` is a Postgres `GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED` column; no application code writes it.
382	- `scan-bundle` keeps download + checksum + manifest parsing in a single `step.run` (Buffer doesn't survive step boundaries).
383	
384	The `shared/extensions/state.ts` module owns every transition of `extensionVersions.status`, `files.scanStatus`, and `extensions.visibility`. Ported verbatim from the original.
385	
386	---
387	
388	## 8. Search
389	
390	Postgres FTS with `pg_trgm` fallback for short fuzzy queries. **Migration SQL is portable verbatim from `../agentcenter/drizzle/0002_fts_search_vector.sql`.**
391	
392	```sql
393	CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
394	
395	ALTER TABLE extensions ADD COLUMN search_vector tsvector
396	  GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
397	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(name, '')),       'A') ||
398	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(name_zh, '')),    'A') ||
399	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(tagline, '')),    'B') ||
400	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(tagline_zh, '')), 'B') ||
401	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(description, '')),    'C') ||
402	    setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(description_zh, '')), 'C')
403	  ) STORED;
404	
405	CREATE INDEX idx_ext_search ON extensions USING GIN (search_vector);
406	CREATE INDEX idx_ext_name_trgm ON extensions USING GIN (lower(name) gin_trgm_ops);
407	CREATE INDEX idx_ext_name_zh_trgm ON extensions USING GIN (name_zh gin_trgm_ops);
408	```
409	
410	`buildExtensionWhere` / `buildExtensionOrder` in `shared/search/query.ts` compose Drizzle SQL clauses from filters; they're pure (no DB call), unit-tested, and shared with `server/api/v1/extensions` so web and CLI see the same listing semantics.
411	
412	Filters originate as `useRoute().query`, parsed by Zod (`shared/validators/filters.ts`) — so the URL is the filter state (shareable, server-rendered, deeplinkable). The `useFilters` composable wraps parse + serialize and exposes `update(partial)` that calls `router.replace` with the new query string.
413

A Vitest suite in `tests/contract/` asserts each `v1` response shape against the example payloads in `docs/api.md` to catch accidental contract drift.

480	
481	## 11. Validate pipeline
482	
483	`bun run validate` is the primary command — the fast inner loop that mirrors the first four steps of CI. It chains four steps in order, failing fast. The fifth gate, `bun run test:integration`, runs PGlite-backed repository tests; CI runs it on every PR but it's not part of `validate` (kept separate so the local typecheck/test loop stays under a few seconds). Phase 0 landed a working `bun run validate` against the bare scaffold; every subsequent phase keeps it green.
484	
485	```bash
486	bun run prepare           # nuxi prepare — generates .nuxt/types/* (needed for typecheck)
487	bun run lint              # @nuxt/eslint over the whole tree
488	bun run typecheck         # nuxi typecheck (vue-tsc) — handles .ts, .vue, auto-imports
489	bun run test              # vitest run — unit + contract suites
490	bun run test:integration  # vitest run -c vitest.config.integration.ts — PGlite repo suite (separate, slower)
491	```
492	
493	### Tools
494	
495	| Step | Tool | Why |
496	|---|---|---|
497	| Prepare | `nuxi prepare` | Generates type shims for auto-imports (`useFetch`, `useAsyncData`, `definePageMeta`, components, composables). Without it, `vue-tsc` errors on every auto-imported symbol. CI must run this before `typecheck`. |
498	| Lint | `@nuxt/eslint` | Auto-configures ESLint rules for Vue 3 + TS + Nuxt 4. Replaces `eslint-config-next`. |
499	| Typecheck | `nuxi typecheck` → `vue-tsc` | `tsc --noEmit` doesn't understand `.vue` SFCs. `vue-tsc` is the wrapper that does. |
500	| Unit / component tests | Vitest + `@nuxt/test-utils` + `@vue/test-utils` + happy-dom | Vitest is the runner; `@vue/test-utils` for `mount()`; `@nuxt/test-utils` for components that touch Nuxt runtime (auto-imports, `useFetch`, `useNuxtApp`) via `mountSuspended()`. |
501	| Integration | Vitest + PGlite (`@electric-sql/pglite` + `drizzle-orm/pglite`) | In-process Postgres-in-WASM with real Drizzle migrations applied. Covers `server/repositories/**` — same SQL dialect as production, no Docker. Runs as a separate suite via `bun run test:integration`. |
502	| E2E | Playwright | Same library as the original. Runs against a dev server with seeded data. Local on demand + nightly CI; **not** per-PR. |
503	
504	### What gets tested where
505	
506	Five tiers, each with a distinct boundary. Together they cover the codebase end-to-end without leaning on any single layer past its strengths.
507	
508	- **Pure unit** (`shared/**/*.test.ts`, `app/**/*.nuxt.test.ts`) — pure logic, validators, composables, components. Vitest, no DB, no real network. Includes the *decisions* extracted from server orchestrators: `shared/extensions/state.ts` (`decideScanOutcome`, `decidePublishOutcome`), `shared/installs/record.ts` (`pickInstallVersion`). Highest leverage, cheapest to write.
509	- **Integration** (`tests/integration/repositories/*.test.ts`) — every function in `server/repositories/**` exercised against PGlite with real Drizzle migrations applied. PGlite is Postgres-in-WASM: same SQL dialect as production, in-process, no Docker. This tier is where SQL is verified — generated columns, FTS, `pg_trgm`, dotted-path `LIKE`, transaction semantics.
510	- **Orchestrator unit** (`server/utils/*.test.ts`, `server/api/**/*.test.ts`) — adapter logic that composes repository calls inside transactions. The **repository module is mocked**, never Drizzle's builder. Verifies orchestration shape (which repo methods get called, in what order, with what arguments), error mapping, and transaction wiring. Fast.
511	- **Contract** (`tests/contract/*.test.ts`) — Zod schemas assert that the JSON payloads documented in `docs/api.md` parse against each `/api/v1` endpoint's response shape. Shape-only, no DB. Catches accidental contract drift before the CLI does.
512	- **E2E** (`tests/e2e/*.spec.ts`) — Playwright against a dev server with seeded data. Owns full-stack flows. Slow, not per-PR.
513	
514	The structural rule that makes the tiers coherent: **Drizzle's query builder is called only inside `server/repositories/`**. Every other layer (`server/utils/`, `server/api/`, jobs) takes a `Transactable` (= `PostgresJsDatabase | PgTransaction`) and calls named repository functions. Transactions are opened at orchestrator boundaries and the `tx` is threaded down through repo calls. Without this rule, "mock the repo" devolves into "mock Drizzle chains" — coupling tests to query implementation and bypassing the Postgres-specific features the integration tier is the only place to verify.
515	
516	### CI
517	
518	`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `bun run validate` plus the integration suite on every PR push:
519	
520	```yaml
521	- bun install --frozen-lockfile
522	- bun run prepare
523	- bun run lint
524	- bun run typecheck
525	- bun run test                # main Vitest suite (unit + contract)
526	- bun run test:integration    # PGlite repository suite
527	```
528	
529	`bun run validate` itself stays fast (no PGlite) — the integration suite is a separate script. CI runs both per-PR; local devs run `test:integration` when touching repositories or schema.
530	
531	A nightly `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` runs Playwright against a seeded test database. Slow + needs DB + browser, so not on every PR.
532	
533	### Locked tooling decisions
534	
535	- **`vue-tsc` is the typechecker.** Do not try to substitute `tsc --noEmit`; it can't read `.vue`. The `bun run typecheck` script wraps `nuxi typecheck`.
536	- **`nuxi prepare` runs before `typecheck` and `lint`.** It's idempotent and fast; always include it. CI must run it after `bun install`.
537	- **Drizzle is only imported inside `server/repositories/`.** Every other layer takes a `Transactable` and calls repo functions. Mocking the Drizzle builder is banned — refactor the call into a repo function and mock that instead. Repository functions themselves are integration-tested against PGlite, never mocked.
538	- **PGlite is the integration DB.** Same SQL dialect as production, in-process, ~50ms cold-start. Commit 2 of P21 includes a smoke check exercising the Postgres-specific features this app uses most: `tsvector` / FTS, `pg_trgm`, dotted-path `LIKE`. If any of these fail on PGlite, fall back to a Docker Postgres service container — but only if needed; the default is PGlite.
539	- **`test:integration` is not part of `validate`.** It's a separate, slower gate (still per-PR in CI). Local devs run it explicitly when touching `server/repositories/**` or `shared/db/schema/**`. Same rationale as Playwright before it: keep the local validate loop tight.
540	- **Playwright is not part of `validate`.** It's a separate, slower gate. Run locally with `bun run test:e2e` on demand; CI runs nightly.
541	
542	---
543	
544	## 12. Coverage & maintainability
545	
546	The original Next.js project relied on culture ("add a colocated test") for test coverage, with no CI threshold. This rewrite tightens that: coverage is a CI gate, with per-area thresholds calibrated to where logic lives. The goal is a codebase that survives 30k+ LOC without regressing into "we don't really test that" rot.
547	
548	### Coverage thresholds (CI-enforced)
549	
550	| Area | Lines | Branches | Why |
551	|---|---|---|---|
552	| `shared/**` (pure logic) | **≥ 95%** | **≥ 90%** | Validators, search query builder, state machine, utilities. Highest leverage; cheapest to test; load-bearing. |
553	| `app/composables/**` | ≥ 90% | ≥ 85% | Mostly pure (filter parse/serialize, tag-label resolver). |
554	| `server/repositories/**` | ≥ 90% | ≥ 85% | Drizzle lives only here. Coverage comes from the integration suite (PGlite). |
555	| `server/utils/**` | ≥ 85% | ≥ 80% | Orchestrators over repos + helpers (auth, storage, inngest). Coverage from unit tests with mocked repos. DB client singleton excluded. |
556	| `server/api/**` | ≥ 70% | ≥ 65% | Endpoints are thin adapters; logic lives in `shared/` or `server/utils/`. End-to-end behavior covered by Playwright. |
557	| `app/components/**` | ≥ 60% overall; ≥ 80% for interactive components (FilterBar, UploadWizard, InstallButton) | — | Component logic that branches on state earns its own tests; pure-layout components are covered by Playwright. |
558	| `app/pages/**`, `app/layouts/**`, `app/app.vue` | excluded | — | Composition only; Playwright owns this layer. |
559	| `cli/**` | unchanged from original | — | Carried over with its existing tests. |
560	
561	Configured in `vitest.config.ts`. The `include` list deliberately scopes coverage measurement to the *currently tested* surface — files not yet in the test pyramid (`server/api/**`, `server/utils/{auth,db,storage,inngest,publish}.ts`, `server/utils/jobs/**`, `server/utils/queries/**`, `app/pages/**`, `app/components/{extension,filters,publish,ui}/**`, layout components without tests) stay outside the include so they're not silently averaged in at 0%. Add a path to `include` only after its tests actually land.
562	
563	```ts
564	test: {
565	  coverage: {
566	    provider: "v8",
567	    reporter: ["text", "html", "lcov"],
568	    include: [
569	      "shared/validators/**",
570	      "shared/search/**",
571	      "shared/extensions/**",
572	      "shared/installs/**",
573	      "shared/tags.ts",
574	      "shared/taxonomy.ts",
575	      "shared/theme.ts",
576	      "app/composables/useFilters.ts",
577	      "app/composables/usePublishWizard.ts",
578	      "app/composables/useTheme.ts",
579	      "server/utils/extensions-state.ts",
580	      "server/utils/installs.ts",
581	    ],
582	    exclude: ["**/*.test.ts", "**/*.spec.ts", ".nuxt/**", ".output/**"],
583	    thresholds: {
584	      lines: 85, branches: 75, functions: 85, statements: 85,
585	      "shared/validators/**":   { lines: 95, branches: 90, functions: 95, statements: 95 },
586	      "shared/search/**":       { lines: 95, branches: 87, functions: 95, statements: 95 },
587	      "shared/extensions/**":   { lines: 95, branches: 90, functions: 95, statements: 95 },
588	      "shared/installs/**":     { lines: 95, branches: 90, functions: 95, statements: 95 },
589	      "shared/tags.ts":         { lines: 95, branches: 90, functions: 95, statements: 95 },
590	      "shared/taxonomy.ts":     { lines: 95, branches: 90, functions: 95, statements: 95 },
591	      "shared/theme.ts":        { lines: 95, branches: 90, functions: 95, statements: 95 },
592	      "server/utils/extensions-state.ts": { lines: 95, branches: 90, functions: 95, statements: 95 },
593	      "server/utils/installs.ts":         { lines: 95, branches: 85, functions: 95, statements: 95 },
594	      "app/composables/useFilters.ts":      { lines: 90, branches: 75, functions: 90, statements: 90 },
595	      "app/composables/usePublishWizard.ts": { lines: 90, branches: 85, functions: 85, statements: 85 },
596	      "app/composables/useTheme.ts":         { lines: 90, branches: 85, functions: 90, statements: 90 },
597	    },
598	  },
599	}
600	```
601	
602	`server/repositories/**` coverage is computed by the integration suite (PGlite). The integration suite's `vitest.config.integration.ts` does not yet emit coverage by default — merging into the main lcov is a CI-side concern. Today the integration suite verifies behavior; the threshold for `server/repositories/**` is enforced de facto by "every repo function has integration test coverage" rather than a numeric gate. Adding the numeric gate is a follow-up.
603	
604	CI runs `bun run test:coverage` and uploads the HTML report as a build artifact. A PR that drops any thresholded subdir below its gate fails CI; reviewers don't have to remember to check. Aspirational thresholds in the table above (e.g. `server/api/**: 70`, `app/components/**: 60–80`) land as those surfaces get test coverage in future PRs.
605	
606	### Patch coverage rule
607	
608	Coverage thresholds protect the aggregate; patch coverage protects each PR from sneaking in untested code under a high-coverage average. Rule:
609	
610	> A PR cannot reduce coverage of any file it touches by more than 3 percentage points.
611	
612	Enforced in CI by diffing `lcov.info` between the PR head and `main`. Practically: if you change a function, you either keep its existing test coverage or add tests to compensate.
613	
614	### TypeScript strictness
615	
616	Beyond `strict: true` (already locked), enable:
617	
618	- **`noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`** — `arr[i]` returns `T | undefined`. Forces handling the missing case. The single change that catches the most "but it always exists" bugs.
619	- **`noImplicitOverride: true`** — `override` keyword required when overriding parent methods. Cheap, catches refactor mistakes.
620	
621	**`exactOptionalPropertyTypes` was tried and dropped in P15.** Vue's `defineProps` adds explicit `undefined` to optional prop types, and reka-ui's prop-forwarding helpers (`useForwardProps`, `useForwardPropsEmits`) then route those values into reka-ui's stricter optional props, which refuse explicit `undefined`. The result is dozens of `TS2379` errors at every shadcn-vue forwarding boundary. The fix would be either casting at each forward site or relaxing the flag globally — the former is verbose and ts-ignorant; the latter loses the "JSON-serializer-shape-drift" guarantee that motivated the flag. Since the marketplace doesn't have a hot JSON-shape-drift path that this flag was preventing, the trade favoured relaxing.
622	
623	These cost ~1 extra hour of TS friction per phase and pay it back the first time a `(items[0] as Item).foo` would have crashed in production.
624	
625	### Layer boundaries
626	
627	The directory layout encodes a dependency graph. Enforce it in ESLint so violations get caught at write time:
628	
629	```text
630	shared/                              ──►  (nothing else)                # leaf — pure code, no framework, no Drizzle
631	server/repositories/                 ──►  shared/db/schema, drizzle-orm  # the ONLY place Drizzle is imported
632	server/utils/, server/api/, server/plugins/, server/jobs/
633	                                     ──►  server/repositories/, shared/  # take Transactable; never import drizzle-orm
634	app/                                 ──►  shared/                        # may import shared/, not server/ (only $fetch over the wire)
635	cli/                                 ──►  (its own world)                # standalone Bun workspace; only talks to /api/v1
636	```
637	
638	`eslint.config.mjs` uses `no-restricted-imports` with glob patterns:
639	
640	```js
641	{
642	  files: ["app/**"],
643	  rules: { "no-restricted-imports": ["error", { patterns: ["server/*", "~~/server/*"] }] },
644	},
645	{
646	  files: ["server/**"],
647	  ignores: ["server/repositories/**", "server/utils/db.ts", "server/plugins/db.ts"],
648	  rules: {
649	    "no-restricted-imports": [
650	      "error",
651	      { patterns: ["app/*", "~/*", "drizzle-orm", "drizzle-orm/*"] },
652	    ],
653	  },
654	},
655	{
656	  files: ["server/repositories/**", "server/utils/db.ts", "server/plugins/db.ts"],
657	  rules: { "no-restricted-imports": ["error", { patterns: ["app/*", "~/*"] }] },
658	},
659	{
660	  files: ["shared/**"],
661	  rules: {
662	    "no-restricted-imports": [
663	      "error",
664	      { patterns: ["app/*", "server/*", "~/*", "~~/server/*", "drizzle-orm", "drizzle-orm/*"] },
665	    ],
666	  },
667	},
668	```
669	
670	The `server/**` rule with `ignores` ensures Drizzle imports outside `server/repositories/`, `server/utils/db.ts`, and `server/plugins/db.ts` are rejected at lint time. This is what makes the repository boundary load-bearing rather than a convention.
671	
672	This is the single rule that keeps the codebase navigable as it grows. Without it, `shared/` slowly grows imports from `server/`, then `app/`, then nothing is testable in isolation.
673	
674	### Other lint rules
675	
676	- **`@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: error`** — `any` is a code smell. Document exceptions with `// reason: ...` directly above the `any`.
677	- **`@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises: error`** — unawaited `$fetch()` calls are the #1 source of "why didn't my mutation happen" bugs.
678	- **`vue/multi-word-component-names: error`** — Vue best practice; avoids collisions with HTML elements.
679	- **`vue/no-unused-refs: error`**, **`vue/require-explicit-emits: error`** — common Vue trapdoors.
680	- **No barrel files** (`index.ts` re-exports) — direct imports from source. Hurts tree-shaking; causes circular imports. The single allowed exception is `shared/db/schema/index.ts` because Drizzle needs the `schema` namespace as a single module.
681	
682	### Test types in this repo
683	
684	| Layer | Test type | Tool |
685	|---|---|---|
686	| `shared/**` pure logic | Unit | Vitest |
687	| `app/composables/**` | Unit (pure) or via consuming component (Nuxt internals) | Vitest + `@nuxt/test-utils/runtime` |
688	| `app/components/**` | Component | Vitest + `@vue/test-utils` + `mountSuspended()` |
689	| `server/repositories/**` | Integration | Vitest + PGlite (`@electric-sql/pglite` + `drizzle-orm/pglite`) |
690	| `server/utils/**`, `server/api/**` | Orchestrator unit (repo mocked, not Drizzle) | Vitest |
691	| `/api/v1/**` JSON shapes | Contract | Vitest, asserts `docs/api.md` payloads against Zod schemas |
692	| End-to-end | E2E | Playwright, seeded DB |
693	
694	### Per-phase coverage discipline
695	
696	Each phase PR ships:
697	
698	1. The feature.
699	2. Tests for any new `shared/**` code at the ≥ 95% line threshold.
700	3. Tests for any new endpoint adapter logic via extracted pure functions.
701	4. Component tests for any new interactive component (forms, multi-step flows, anything with branching state).
702	5. A Playwright spec update if the feature is reachable from a new URL.
703	
704	Reviewers reject PRs that ship `shared/**` code without unit tests. This is a hard rule, not a "would be nice." The cost of letting one through is the seed of "we don't really test that area" — easier to never start.
705	
706	### What this does not include
707	
708	Deliberately out of scope for v1:
709	
710	- **Mutation testing** (Stryker): high-value but slow to wire; revisit at v2 if coverage starts feeling like vanity.
711	- **Visual regression** (Playwright screenshots): defer to P13 polish; needs a stable design first.
712	- **Storybook / Histoire** for component documentation: defer; not load-bearing for a v1 codebase.
713	- **External coverage trend service** (Codecov, Coveralls): the local-first deploy target rules out per-PR third-party uploads as a hard dependency. CI artifact is sufficient.
714	
715	---
716	
717	## 13. Commit & PR rules
718	
719	The original Next.js project locked "Conventional Commits, one coherent unit per commit, phase scope." That carries over verbatim. This section spells out the parts that were left informal — granularity, breaking-change handling for `/api/v1`, merge strategy, the per-commit vs. per-PR validate split, and the hook tooling.
720	
721	### Commit message format
722	
723	```
724	<type>(<scope>): <one-line summary, lowercase, no trailing period>
725	
726	<body — optional. Why, not what. Wraps at 72 chars.
727	Reference incidents, surprising decisions, or invariants the diff doesn't show.>
728	
729	<footer — optional. BREAKING CHANGE, Closes #N, …>
730	```
731	
732	### Types
733	
734	`feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`, `perf`, `revert`, `style`. Use the type that describes the dominant change in the commit. A commit that's "feat plus its tests" is `feat`, not split.
735	
736	### Scopes
737	
738	Two scope shapes used here:
739	
740	- **Phase scope** during the v1 build: `p<N>-<short>` matching §10. Example: `feat(p3-browse): wire filter chips to query string`. Use this for any commit that lands a phase deliverable.
741	- **Feature scope** for hotfixes during v1 and all post-v1 work: a short noun for the area touched. Examples: `fix(filter-bar): preserve dept on locale switch`, `refactor(install-button): extract install state machine`, `chore(deps): bump drizzle 0.45 → 0.46`.
742	
743	If a commit spans two scopes evenly, that's a smell — split it.
744	
745	### Commit granularity — one coherent unit per commit
746	
747	A phase is one or several commits. Default to **one coherent unit per commit** — a single focused change that compiles and stands on its own. The exact number of commits per phase depends on the work: a mechanical port may be one commit per phase; a feature build may be several. Optimise for "the diff tells a clear story", not for a target commit count.
748	
749	Calibration:
750	
751	| Granularity | Example | Verdict |
752	|---|---|---|
753	| Too small | `feat: rename variable in ext-card.vue` | No — file-by-file noise |
754	| Right | `chore(p0): install @nuxt/eslint and base config` | Yes |
755	| Right | `feat(p2-db): add extension drizzle schema` | Yes |
756	| Right | `feat(p3-browse): ExtCard component + test` | Yes — code + its tests usually one commit |
757	| Right | `feat(p3-browse): wire ExtCard into home grid` | Yes |
758	| Right | `feat(p15-ui): port shadcn-vue primitives` covering ~28 generated wrappers (Button + Input + Label + Textarea + Checkbox + Skeleton + Dialog × 6 + Sheet × 4 + Popover × 3 + Select × 5 + Tabs × 4) | Yes — single mechanical unit |
759	| Too big | `feat(p3-browse): browse page` covering 8 unrelated files | No — split where the story changes |
760	
761	Tests usually live with the code they cover in the same commit. The exception is adding tests to *existing* code as a coverage-improvement pass — then the test commit stands alone.
762	
763	Always-split boundaries (these go in separate commits even if "small"):
764	
765	- Database schema / migration vs. application code that uses it.
766	- Refactor vs. new feature (refactor first; feature on top).
767	- Generated code (migrations, lockfile updates) vs. source.
768	- Dependency install (`chore`) vs. first use (`feat`).
769	
770	### Per-commit vs. per-PR validate
771	
772	The validate suite has two gates with different strictness:
773	
774	- **Each commit must compile and `bun run typecheck` must pass.** This is the per-step gate. Strict enough to keep history bisectable; loose enough that you can land a Zod validator in one commit before its consumer in the next.
775	- **The PR head must pass full `bun run validate`** (lint + typecheck + test + coverage thresholds). This is the per-PR gate. Enforced by the `pre-push` hook locally and by CI on the PR.
776	
777	This split is intentional. Trying to make every single commit hit 95% coverage on `shared/**` would force unnatural test-first-then-code ordering. Coverage is a PR-boundary property, not a commit-boundary property.
778	
779	### Breaking changes
780	
781	The `/api/v1` contract is the only thing in this repo that can break external consumers (the CLI). If you change a v1 endpoint's response shape, request shape, or status semantics, mark the commit with both `!` and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer:
782	
783	```
784	feat(p7-api)!: bundle endpoint returns 410 for archived versions
785	
786	BREAKING CHANGE: GET /api/v1/extensions/:slug/bundle previously returned 503
787	for archived versions; it now returns 410 Gone. CLI < 0.3.0 will misinterpret
788	this. Bump the CLI minimum and document the upgrade in cli/CHANGELOG.md.
789	```
790	
791	CI's contract suite (`tests/contract/`) fails when a v1 response shape changes without these markers — a hard gate, not a convention. Anything else (internal endpoints, components, schema before v1.0 ships) doesn't need the marker; update `docs/plan.md` instead.
792	
793	### Hard rules
794	
795	- **No `--amend` once a commit is on a pushed branch.** Pushed history is shared. Local pre-push amends are fine.
796	- **No `--force` / `--force-with-lease`** on pushed branches. Use a corrective commit (`fix: the previous commit broke X`) or `revert` instead.
797	- **No `--no-verify`.** If a hook is wrong, fix the hook in its own commit; don't bypass.
798	- **No squash-then-amend dance to "clean up" a PR.** PRs are reviewed and merged with their commit history intact. A 20-noisy-commits PR is a PR-shape problem, not a history-cleanup problem — split the work earlier.
799	
800	### Merge strategy
801	
802	PRs merge as **merge commits**, not squash, not rebase. Each phase's commit history is preserved on `main`.
803	
804	Rationale:
805	
806	- The phase-internal commit split exists for a reason — squashing a phase into one commit destroys that.
807	- `git log --first-parent main` gives the high-level view (one entry per merged PR); `git log main` gives the per-commit detail. Both are useful.
808	- `git bisect` is more precise with smaller commits visible on `main`.
```

## Auth & Authorization Model Report: agentcenter-nuxt

### 1. Better Auth Setup

**Server-side config** (`/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/utils/auth.ts:14-46`):
- Better Auth instance created as lazy singleton with Drizzle PostgreSQL adapter
- Email/password auth enabled
- Three additional user fields via `additionalFields` (input: false): `locale`, `themePreference`, `defaultDeptId`

**User table schema** (`/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/auth.ts:9-23`):
- Standard Better Auth columns: id (PK), email (unique), emailVerified, name, image
- Plus custom fields: bio, locale, themePreference, defaultDeptId (logical reference to departments, no FK)
- Timestamps: createdAt, updatedAt

**Client-side**: Browser auth uses `createAuthClient()` from better-auth/vue in `/app/composables/useAuth.ts`. Server-side and middleware calls pass `fetchOptions.headers` with cookies explicitly to work across SSR boundaries.

### 2. Existing Authorization Patterns

**No role column or isAdmin flag exists on users table.** Authorization is minimal:
- `requireUser(event)` (`/server/utils/auth.ts:80-86`): throws 401 if session missing; used on all web API endpoints (`/api/internal/*`)
- `getSessionUser(event)`: returns user or null
- No `requireOwner` or `requireAdmin` helpers found

**Representative endpoint** (`/server/api/internal/installs.post.ts`): calls `requireUser()`, then records install with userId. Authorization is implicit — only authenticated users can install.

**CLI auth** (`/server/utils/api-auth.ts:12-31`): `authenticateBearerToken(event)` joins sessions → users on Bearer token, returns `{id, email, name, defaultDeptId}`.

### 3. Organizations / Departments

**Org/membership schema** (`/shared/db/schema/org.ts`):
- **organizations** table: id (PK), slug, name, nameZh, logoUrl
- **departments** table: dotted-path id PK (e.g. "eng.cloud.infra"), orgId (FK), parentId, name, nameZh, pathDepth; indexed on id (text_pattern_ops) for LIKE '%parent%' queries
- **memberships** table: userId (FK users), orgId (FK orgs), deptId (FK depts), role enum {viewer, publisher, admin}

**Department structure** (seed data at `/shared/data/departments.ts`): three top-level depts (eng, biz, ops) each with nested children. Seed script (`/scripts/seed.ts:44-62`) flattens the tree, computing pathDepth for each. The comment at line 58-59 notes departments will eventually be user-selected via `user.defaultDeptId` (currently hardcoded to "eng.cloud.infra").

**No org/membership access control** in `/api/internal/` endpoints yet — memberships table is seeded but not queried in any current handler.

### 4. Routing Middleware

**Client middleware** (`/app/middleware/`):
- `require-auth.ts`: redirects unauthenticated users to `/sign-in?next=<path>` (named, opted-in via `definePageMeta`)
- `require-onboard.ts` (referenced in `/app/pages/profile.vue`): redirects if `user.defaultDeptId` is null to `/onboard`
- `legacy-categories.global.ts`: URL canonicalization (global)

**No server-side middleware** directory exists; auth gating is inline in handlers.

### 5. Profile / Settings Pages

**Single profile page**: `/app/pages/profile.vue` (requires both "require-auth" and "require-onboard" middleware)
- Sections: installed, published, drafts, saved, collections, activity, **settings**
- Settings form (`ProfileSettingsForm`) allows editing name, bio, defaultDeptId, created_at display
- Fetches from `/api/internal/profile/{me,section}` endpoints

**No dedicated `/admin` area exists.** The app currently has no admin UI for managing departments, organizations, or user roles. Seed data is manual (`scripts/seed.ts`).

---

## Summary (350 words)

The agentcenter-nuxt app uses **Better Auth** with PostgreSQL/Drizzle, storing sessions and users in a standard schema. The `users` table has no role/admin flag; authorization is minimal—only `requireUser()` checks exist on `/api/internal` endpoints, with no resource ownership or role-based guards.

**Organization & membership infrastructure is in place** (`organizations`, `departments`, `memberships` tables with role enum) and seeded, but **unused in the application layer**. No endpoint queries memberships yet. Departments are populated with a dotted-path structure (e.g. "eng.cloud.infra") to support hierarchical access control, and users have a `defaultDeptId` field, but department-scoped authorization is not implemented. The `/onboard` middleware checks that `defaultDeptId` is set but does not restrict access based on membership.

**Client routing is straightforward**: `require-auth` and `require-onboard` named middleware protect the `/profile` page. There is no `/admin` or `/settings` dedicated route; both are tabs within `/profile`. No admin UI exists for managing departments or users; all org/dept setup happens via `scripts/seed.ts`.

**Device-code flow** (`/api/v1/auth/device/*`) backs CLI authentication with the same `sessions` table, gated by bearer token via `authenticateBearerToken()`.

The gap is clear: the schema supports multi-org, multi-role access control (per Decision #9 on departments), but endpoints do not enforce it. Authorization is user-centric, not resource-centric. Next phases would need to add membership-based guards, department hierarchical queries (using LIKE against dotted paths), and admin routes for org/dept management.

## Pattern Discovery Report: AgentCenter-Nuxt

### 1. **I18n Column-Per-Language Pattern (Decision #10)**

**Column Naming Convention: `name` + `nameZh` (or domain-specific name + `Zh` variant)**

Found in 3 major tables:
- **extensions**: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/extension.ts:100-105`
  - `name` / `nameZh`, `tagline` / `taglineZh`, `description` / `descriptionZh`, `changelog` / `changelogZh`
  
- **organizations**: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/org.ts:23-24`
  - `name` / `nameZh`
  
- **departments**: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/org.ts:41-42`
  - `name` / `nameZh` (both required)
  
- **collections**: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/collection.ts:32-35`
  - `name` / `nameZh`, `description` / `descriptionZh`
  
- **tags**: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/extension.ts:186-187`
  - Uses `labelEn` / `labelZh` (not `label`/`labelZh`, exceptions for enum-like data)

**Locale File Structure:**
- Root: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/i18n/locales/`
  - `en.json` — English translations (default locale)
  - `zh.json` — Chinese translations
- Top-level shape (hierarchical namespacing): `"common"`, `"nav"`, `"home"`, `"publish"`, `"errors"`, etc.
- Character counter constants imported from validators (e.g., `COLLECTION_NAME_MAX` in `/shared/validators/collection.ts:8`)

---

### 2. **Form Validation Pattern**

**Zod Validators (Server truth):** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/validators/`

- **manifest.ts** — `ManifestFormSchema` exports both server (BundleManifestSchema) and client (ManifestFormSchema) shapes
  - Shared patterns: `nameZh` optional, `SUMMARY_MAX=80` constant for inline UI validation
  
- **collection.ts** — `CreateCollectionInput`, `UpdateCollectionInput`, constants like `COLLECTION_NAME_MAX=100`

**Client-Side Usage:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/app/components/publish/WizardBasics.vue`
- Two-way bind form state directly to imported `ManifestFormValues` type
- No dedicated vee-validate component wrapping; bare input elements with v-model
- i18n labels via `t()` composable (e.g., `t('publish.fields.name')`)

**API Handlers** (pattern example): `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/api/internal/publish/submit.post.ts:4-6`
- Parse body with Zod schema, throw createError with HTTP status map for validation failures
- No centralized error message localization at the validation layer; messages live in i18n locale files

---

### 3. **Inngest Events**

**Registration & Functions:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/utils/inngest.ts`
- Singleton client: `new Inngest({ id: "agentcenter" })`
- Lazy-loaded functions in `getInngestFunctions()` to avoid bundle bloat

**Existing Events:**
- `extension/scan.requested` → `/server/utils/jobs/scan-bundle.ts:19-121`
- `extension/index.requested` → `/server/utils/jobs/reindex-search.ts:7-42`
- `extension/published` (internal event, not a trigger)

**Emission Pattern** (example): `/server/utils/publish.ts:348-353`
```
await inngest.send({
  name: "extension/scan.requested",
  data: { versionId, fileId }
})
```
Event data validated via Zod schemas inside each function's handler.

---

### 4. **Notification / Email Patterns**

**No existing email or in-app notification system found.** The codebase has:
- Activity table (`installs`, `ratings`): `/shared/db/schema/activity.ts` — records user actions but no notification/audit log table
- Inngest events for workflow state transitions but no notification bus
- Comments in code suggest email/audit logging are future concerns

**Closest pattern: Version state machine** (`extensions-state.ts`) transitions versions through states (`pending` → `scanning` → `ready`/`rejected`) and fires Inngest events at transition points, but there's no subscriber listening for notifications.

---

**Key takeaway for extension approval workflow:** Follow the state-machine + Inngest event pattern already in use for version scanning. Create an `approval_status` enum on extensions, transition it via a state manager function, and emit events like `extension/approval.requested` and `extension/approval.completed`. Reuse the `nameZh`/`name` column pair pattern and add validator constants to `shared/validators/` for any new form inputs.

1	// Pure decision functions for the extension state machine. The server-side
2	// orchestrator (`server/utils/extensions-state.ts`) calls these to figure
3	// out *what* to write; the orchestrator itself owns the *how* (loading
4	// rows, opening transactions, calling repositories). Keeping the
5	// decisions here means they're testable with no DB and no mocks — just
6	// inputs → outputs.
7	
8	export type ExtensionScope = "personal" | "org" | "enterprise"
9	
10	export type ScanResult =
11	  | { ok: true; checksum: string; scanReport: unknown }
12	  | { ok: false; reason: string; scanReport: unknown }
13	
14	export type FileScanUpdate =
15	  | { scanStatus: "clean"; scanReport: unknown; checksumSha256: string }
16	  | { scanStatus: "flagged"; scanReport: unknown }
17	
18	export type VersionStatusUpdate =
19	  | { status: "ready"; publishedAt: Date | null }
20	  | { status: "rejected" }
21	
22	export interface ExtensionPublishedUpdate {
23	  visibility: "published"
24	  publishedAt: Date
25	}
26	
27	export interface ScanDecision {
28	  file: FileScanUpdate
29	  version: VersionStatusUpdate
30	  // Present iff this scan should also flip the parent extension to
31	  // `published` (personal scope + ok result). Absent otherwise.
32	  extension?: ExtensionPublishedUpdate
33	}
34	
35	// Decide the row updates from a scan outcome. The parent extension is
36	// only flipped to `published` when the scope is `personal` and the scan
37	// succeeded — org/enterprise scans always wait for an admin
38	// `publishVersion` call regardless of the result.
39	export function decideScanOutcome(input: {
40	  scope: ExtensionScope
41	  result: ScanResult
42	  now: Date
43	}): ScanDecision {
44	  const { scope, result, now } = input
45	
46	  if (!result.ok) {
47	    return {
48	      file: { scanStatus: "flagged", scanReport: result.scanReport },
49	      version: { status: "rejected" },
50	    }
51	  }
52	
53	  const isPersonal = scope === "personal"
54	  const publishedAt = isPersonal ? now : null
55	
56	  const decision: ScanDecision = {
57	    file: {
58	      scanStatus: "clean",
59	      scanReport: result.scanReport,
60	      checksumSha256: result.checksum,
61	    },
62	    version: { status: "ready", publishedAt },
63	  }
64	
65	  if (isPersonal) {
66	    decision.extension = { visibility: "published", publishedAt: now }
67	  }
68	
69	  return decision
70	}
71	
72	export interface PublishDecision {
73	  extension: ExtensionPublishedUpdate
74	  // Just a `publishedAt` stamp — `status` stays `ready`.
75	  version: { publishedAt: Date }
76	}
77	
78	// Admin publish flow: stamp both the extension and the version with the
79	// same `now` so their `publishedAt` line up.
80	export function decidePublishOutcome(now: Date): PublishDecision {
81	  return {
82	    extension: { visibility: "published", publishedAt: now },
83	    version: { publishedAt: now },
84	  }
85	}
86	
```

## Approved Plan:
# Official-tier approval workflow

## Context

Today every published extension is treated the same: there's a hand-curated
`badge` enum column (`official | popular | new`) on `extensions`, but no
process ever writes to it — it exists only for editorial seeding. The product
now needs a real moderation path:

- Extensions default to **Unofficial** when a user uploads them.
- A publisher can apply for elevation to one of two **official tiers**:
  **Product-Line** or **Company**.
- Each (tier × functional category) cell is reviewed by a specific set of
  administrators. The matrix must be **configurable at runtime**, not just
  seeded.

Locked decisions (from this planning session):

1. **Category = `subCat`** (text, drawn from `FUNC_TAXONOMY`).
   There are 9 leaves (`systemDesign`, `softDev`, `testing`, `network`,
   `embedded`, `cloud`, `docs`, `data`, `vcs`), so the matrix has
   `9 subCats × 2 tiers = 18` cells.
2. **Tiers are independent.** A publisher can apply directly for either
   tier; Company supersedes Product-Line if both end up granted.
3. **Status field**: add a new `officialTier` enum (`productLine | company`,
   nullable = "unofficial"). The existing `badge` column is preserved for
   the frozen `/api/v1` contract but is **read-derived** from `officialTier`
   at the API boundary — never written from app code again.
4. **Matrix admin = super-admin only.** Add a `superAdmin` value to
   `membershipRoleEnum`; only super-admins can edit the matrix. Tier
   reviewers handle decisions on their assigned cells but don't edit the
   matrix.

The CLI contract under `/api/v1` is frozen (`docs/plan.md` §13) — this change
must be additive there.

---

## Schema changes (`shared/db/schema/extension.ts`, `org.ts`, new `approval.ts`)

### New enums

```ts
// shared/db/schema/extension.ts
export const officialTierEnum = pgEnum("extension_official_tier", [
  "productLine",
  "company",
]);

// shared/db/schema/approval.ts (new file)
export const approvalStatusEnum = pgEnum("approval_status", [
  "pending",
  "approved",
  "rejected",
  "withdrawn",
]);
```

### `extensions` table

- Add `officialTier: officialTierEnum()` (nullable, default null).
- **Keep** `badge` column and `extensionBadgeEnum` unchanged for now — the
  `/api/v1` response shapes (`docs/api.md:97,127`) include `badge` and
  the CLI may key on it. The repository layer will compute `badge` as a
  derived value (`officialTier ? "official" : extensions.badge`) only in
  the response mappers at `server/api/v1/extensions/index.get.ts:35` and
  `server/api/v1/extensions/[slug]/index.get.ts:24`. App code stops
  writing `badge` entirely; future removal can ride a v2 contract bump.
- Add index `idx_ext_official_tier` on `officialTier` for the filter pill.

### `memberships` table

- Add `"superAdmin"` to `membershipRoleEnum` via `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`.
  Existing roles (`viewer | publisher | admin`) are untouched. A user gains
  super-admin by holding a membership with `role = 'superAdmin'` on the
  default org.

### New table `approval_requests`

```ts
// shared/db/schema/approval.ts
export const approvalRequests = pgTable("approval_requests", {
  id: text().primaryKey(),
  extensionId: text().notNull().references(() => extensions.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  requestedTier: officialTierEnum().notNull(),
  // Snapshot of subCat at submission. Source of truth is FUNC_TAXONOMY;
  // validated server-side against the flattened leaf set.
  subCat: text().notNull(),
  requestedByUserId: text().notNull().references(() => users.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  reason: text(),                      // optional publisher justification
  status: approvalStatusEnum().notNull().default("pending"),
  decidedByUserId: text().references(() => users.id, { onDelete: "set null" }),
  decidedAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }),
  reviewerNote: text(),
  createdAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
}, (t) => [
  // Queue lookup for reviewers
  index("idx_approval_status_cell").on(t.status, t.subCat, t.requestedTier),
  // Publisher's "my requests" view + the at-most-one-pending guard
  index("idx_approval_ext_status").on(t.extensionId, t.status),
]);
```

At-most-one-pending-per-extension is enforced in the orchestrator (race
window covered by opening a transaction and re-checking before insert);
a partial unique index is the natural shape but PG partial indexes don't
read well in PGlite — guard at the orchestrator level instead.

### New table `approval_reviewers` (the matrix)

```ts
export const approvalReviewers = pgTable("approval_reviewers", {
  id: text().primaryKey(),
  tier: officialTierEnum().notNull(),
  subCat: text().notNull(),
  userId: text().notNull().references(() => users.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  createdAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
}, (t) => [
  unique("approval_reviewers_cell_user_unique").on(t.tier, t.subCat, t.userId),
  index("idx_approval_reviewers_cell").on(t.tier, t.subCat),
]);
```

Multiple reviewers per cell; first reviewer to decide wins (no quorum for v1).

### Migration order

Drizzle-kit generates one migration. Hand-edit if needed so the order is:

1. `ALTER TYPE membership_role ADD VALUE 'superAdmin'`
2. `CREATE TYPE extension_official_tier ...`, `CREATE TYPE approval_status ...`
3. `ALTER TABLE extensions ADD COLUMN official_tier ...`
4. `CREATE TABLE approval_requests`, `approval_reviewers` with indexes.

---

## Pure decisions (`shared/approvals/state.ts`, `shared/validators/approvals.ts`)

Mirrors `shared/extensions/state.ts` — pure functions, no DB. Owns every
transition of `approval_requests.status` and the resulting
`extensions.officialTier` update.

```ts
// shared/approvals/state.ts
export type ApprovalDecision =
  | { decision: "approve" }
  | { decision: "reject"; note?: string };

export interface ApprovalOutcome {
  request: {
    status: "approved" | "rejected";
    decidedByUserId: string;
    decidedAt: Date;
    reviewerNote: string | null;
  };
  extension?: { officialTier: "productLine" | "company" };  // present iff approved
}

export function decideApprovalOutcome(input: {
  current: { status: ApprovalStatus; requestedTier: OfficialTier };
  decision: ApprovalDecision;
  reviewerUserId: string;
  now: Date;
}): ApprovalOutcome { /* ... */ }

export function decideWithdrawOutcome(input: { current: { status } }): { status: "withdrawn" } { /* ... */ }
```

Validators in `shared/validators/approvals.ts`:

- `SubmitApprovalSchema` — `extensionId`, `requestedTier`, `subCat` (validated
  against a flattened `Set` of `FUNC_TAXONOMY` `l1.key` values), `reason?`.
- `DecideApprovalSchema` — `requestId`, `decision` ('approve'|'reject'), `note?`.
- `AssignReviewerSchema` — `tier`, `subCat`, `userId`.

Same Zod-shared-with-server pattern as `shared/validators/extension.ts`.

---

## Repositories (`server/repositories/approvals.ts`, `reviewers.ts`)

Drizzle is only imported here (project layer-boundary rule, `docs/plan.md` §11).

- `approvals.ts`: `createRequest`, `findById`, `findPendingByExtension`,
  `listForReviewer(userId, { tier?, subCat?, status? })`,
  `listForPublisher(userId)`, `updateStatus`.
- `reviewers.ts`: `listMatrix()` (returns full 18-cell grid joined with users),
  `assign({tier, subCat, userId})`, `unassign(id)`,
  `findReviewersFor(tier, subCat)`, `isReviewerFor(userId, tier, subCat)`.

Both get PGlite integration tests under `tests/integration/repositories/`.

---

## Orchestrators (`server/utils/approvals.ts`)

Takes `Transactable`, calls repos, opens a transaction at the boundary.

- `submitRequest({ extensionId, requestedTier, subCat, userId, reason })`
  - Guard: extension exists, publisher is owner (`publisherUserId === userId`),
    `visibility === 'published'`, no row in `approval_requests` where
    `extensionId = $1 AND status = 'pending'`.
  - Snapshot `subCat` into the request (don't trust client; if extension has
    no `subCat`, require the form to provide one).
  - Emit Inngest event `extension/approval.requested`
    `{ requestId, extensionId, requestedTier, subCat, requesterUserId }`.
- `decideRequest({ requestId, decision, reviewerUserId, note })`
  - Guard: request is `pending`, reviewer is in `approval_reviewers` for
    `(request.requestedTier, request.subCat)` OR has `role = 'superAdmin'`
    (super-admins can decide anywhere).
  - Apply `decideApprovalOutcome`; if approved, also update
    `extensions.officialTier`.
  - Emit `extension/approval.decided`.
- `withdrawRequest({ requestId, userId })`
  - Guard: requester owns the request, status is `pending`.

Auth helpers in `server/utils/auth.ts`:

- `requireSuperAdmin(event)` — joins `memberships` on the calling user;
  throws 403 if no row with `role = 'superAdmin'`.
- `requireReviewerFor(event, tier, subCat)` — checks `approval_reviewers` OR
  super-admin.

---

## API endpoints (`server/api/internal/`)

All call `requireUser` first (`server/utils/auth.ts:80`); guards beyond that
live in the orchestrators.

```
server/api/internal/approvals/
  submit.post.ts     POST  body: SubmitApprovalSchema       → publisher submits
  withdraw.post.ts   POST  body: { requestId }              → publisher withdraws
  decide.post.ts     POST  body: DecideApprovalSchema       → reviewer decides
  list.get.ts        GET   query: ?view=mine|queue          → list for me as publisher or reviewer

server/api/internal/admin/reviewers/
  index.get.ts       GET   → list matrix (super-admin)
  assign.post.ts     POST  body: AssignReviewerSchema       → super-admin
  unassign.delete.ts DELETE body: { id }                    → super-admin
```

Public `/api/v1` is **not** extended in this PR. `officialTier` lands in
`/api/v1` responses as an additive field only after a contract update —
keep it out of v1 mappers for now, but add it to the response payload in a
follow-up that updates `docs/api.md`. The derived `badge` mapping (above) is
the only `/api/v1` change here, and it preserves the existing shape verbatim.

  story on `main`.

Pause for explicit human checkpoint after commit 4 (server side complete,
schema + API surface usable from curl) before starting commits 5–6 (UI).
This is the natural seam — UI work can be redirected without throwing
schema/server work away.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **`badge` deprecation**: kept for v1 contract compatibility but no longer
  written. Removing the column + enum is a follow-up that bumps `/api/v1`.
- **Notifications**: the Inngest events are emitted but only logged. Email
  / in-app notification fan-out is P1.
- **Revocation**: a super-admin removing a granted tier is not in this
  scope. Adding it later is just an extra `revokeOfficial` orchestrator
  + endpoint — the data model already supports null.
- **Audit log**: this design stores the final decision + note on the
  request row but does not capture intermediate edits to the matrix.
  If audit becomes a requirement, add a separate `audit_events` table
  in a later phase.

```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/db/schema/approval.ts",
  "content": "import {\n  index,\n  pgEnum,\n  pgTable,\n  text,\n  timestamp,\n  unique,\n} from \"drizzle-orm/pg-core\";\n\nimport { users } from \"./auth\";\nimport { extensions, officialTierEnum } from \"./extension\";\n\nexport const approvalStatusEnum = pgEnum(\"approval_status\", [\n  \"pending\",\n  \"approved\",\n  \"rejected\",\n  \"withdrawn\",\n]);\n\nexport const approvalRequests = pgTable(\n  \"approval_requests\",\n  {\n    id: text().primaryKey(),\n    extensionId: text()\n      .notNull()\n      .references(() => extensions.id, { onDelete: \"cascade\" }),\n    requestedTier: officialTierEnum().notNull(),\n    // Snapshot of the functional subCat at submission time. Source of truth is\n    // FUNC_TAXONOMY in shared/taxonomy.ts; validated against the flattened l1\n    // key set at the validator layer.\n    subCat: text().notNull(),\n    requestedByUserId: text()\n      .notNull()\n      .references(() => users.id, { onDelete: \"cascade\" }),\n    reason: text(),\n    status: approvalStatusEnum().notNull().default(\"pending\"),\n    decidedByUserId: text().references(() => users.id, {\n      onDelete: \"set null\",\n    }),\n    decidedAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }),\n    reviewerNote: text(),\n    createdAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),\n    updatedAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),\n  },\n  (t) => [\n    // Reviewer queue: pending rows in a given cell, ordered by createdAt.\n    index(\"idx_approval_status_cell\").on(\n      t.status,\n      t.subCat,\n      t.requestedTier,\n    ),\n    // Publisher \"my requests\" view and the at-most-one-pending guard.\n    index(\"idx_approval_ext_status\").on(t.extensionId, t.status),\n  ],\n);\n\nexport const approvalReviewers = pgTable(\n  \"approval_reviewers\",\n  {\n    id: text().primaryKey(),\n    tier: officialTierEnum().notNull(),\n    // Same FUNC_TAXONOMY l1 key as approvalRequests.subCat — text rather\n    // than enum so adding a taxonomy leaf doesn't require a migration.\n    subCat: text().notNull(),\n    userId: text()\n      .notNull()\n      .references(() => users.id, { onDelete: \"cascade\" }),\n    createdAt: timestamp({ withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),\n  },\n  (t) => [\n    unique(\"approval_reviewers_cell_user_unique\").on(\n      t.tier,\n      t.subCat,\n      t.userId,\n    ),\n    index(\"idx_approval_reviewers_cell\").on(t.tier, t.subCat),\n  ],\n);\n"
}

1	import { z } from "zod"
2	
3	// Input schemas for the collections feature. Mirrors the lightweight,
4	// constant-led style used in `profile.ts` so the API handlers can call
5	// `.parse(raw)` directly and the UI can import the same `_MAX` constants for
6	// inline character counters.
7	export const COLLECTION_NAME_MIN = 1
8	export const COLLECTION_NAME_MAX = 100
9	export const COLLECTION_DESC_MAX = 500
10	
11	export const CollectionVisibility = z.enum(["private", "public"])
12	export type CollectionVisibility = z.infer<typeof CollectionVisibility>
13	
14	export const CreateCollectionInput = z.object({
15	  name: z.string().trim().min(COLLECTION_NAME_MIN).max(COLLECTION_NAME_MAX),
16	  nameZh: z
17	    .string()
18	    .trim()
19	    .max(COLLECTION_NAME_MAX)
20	    .optional()
21	    .transform((v) => (v && v.length > 0 ? v : undefined)),
22	  description: z
23	    .string()
24	    .trim()
25	    .max(COLLECTION_DESC_MAX)
26	    .optional()
27	    .transform((v) => (v && v.length > 0 ? v : undefined)),
28	  descriptionZh: z
29	    .string()
30	    .trim()
31	    .max(COLLECTION_DESC_MAX)
32	    .optional()
33	    .transform((v) => (v && v.length > 0 ? v : undefined)),
34	  visibility: CollectionVisibility.default("private"),
35	})
36	
37	export type CreateCollectionInput = z.infer<typeof CreateCollectionInput>
38	
39	// `.partial()` alone would inherit the `.default("private")` from
40	// CreateCollectionInput.visibility — in Zod v4 the default is materialized
41	// even when the field is omitted, which would silently reset a public
42	// collection to private on every PATCH that didn't touch visibility.
43	// Omit, partial, then re-add visibility as plain optional so an omitted
44	// field stays `undefined` and the repo's `!== undefined` check correctly
45	// skips the column.
46	export const UpdateCollectionInput = CreateCollectionInput
47	  .omit({ visibility: true })
48	  .partial()
49	  .extend({ visibility: CollectionVisibility.optional() })
50	export type UpdateCollectionInput = z.infer<typeof UpdateCollectionInput>
51	
52	export const AddItemInput = z.object({
53	  extensionId: z.string().trim().min(1),
54	})
55	export type AddItemInput = z.infer<typeof AddItemInput>
56

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/approvals/state.ts",
  "content": "// Pure decision functions for the official-tier approval workflow. Mirrors\n// `shared/extensions/state.ts`: the orchestrator\n// (`server/utils/approvals.ts`) calls these to figure out *what* to write;\n// the orchestrator owns the *how* (loading rows, opening transactions,\n// calling repositories). Keeping the decisions here means they're testable\n// with no DB and no mocks — just inputs → outputs.\n\nexport type OfficialTier = \"productLine\" | \"company\"\n\nexport type ApprovalStatus = \"pending\" | \"approved\" | \"rejected\" | \"withdrawn\"\n\nexport type ApprovalAction =\n  | { decision: \"approve\" }\n  | { decision: \"reject\"; note?: string }\n\nexport interface ApprovalRequestPatch {\n  status: \"approved\" | \"rejected\"\n  decidedByUserId: string\n  decidedAt: Date\n  reviewerNote: string | null\n}\n\nexport interface ExtensionOfficialTierPatch {\n  officialTier: OfficialTier\n}\n\nexport interface ApprovalOutcome {\n  request: ApprovalRequestPatch\n  // Present iff the request was approved — the orchestrator stamps the new\n  // tier onto the parent extension in the same transaction.\n  extension?: ExtensionOfficialTierPatch\n}\n\n// Decide the row updates from a reviewer's verdict. Only pending requests\n// can transition; other states are no-ops and throw at the orchestrator.\nexport function decideApprovalOutcome(input: {\n  current: { status: ApprovalStatus; requestedTier: OfficialTier }\n  action: ApprovalAction\n  reviewerUserId: string\n  now: Date\n}): ApprovalOutcome {\n  const { current, action, reviewerUserId, now } = input\n\n  if (current.status !== \"pending\") {\n    throw new Error(\n      `cannot decide approval request in status '${current.status}'`,\n    )\n  }\n\n  if (action.decision === \"approve\") {\n    return {\n      request: {\n        status: \"approved\",\n        decidedByUserId: reviewerUserId,\n        decidedAt: now,\n        reviewerNote: null,\n      },\n      extension: { officialTier: current.requestedTier },\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Reject — note is preserved verbatim; an empty/whitespace-only note\n  // collapses to null so downstream \"if reviewerNote\" reads cleanly.\n  const trimmed = action.note?.trim()\n  return {\n    request: {\n      status: \"rejected\",\n      decidedByUserId: reviewerUserId,\n      decidedAt: now,\n      reviewerNote: trimmed && trimmed.length > 0 ? trimmed : null,\n    },\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface WithdrawOutcome {\n  request: { status: \"withdrawn\"; decidedAt: Date }\n}\n\n// A publisher can withdraw a request while it's still pending. Withdrawal\n// is recorded with a timestamp but no reviewer, since no admin acted.\nexport function decideWithdrawOutcome(input: {\n  current: { status: ApprovalStatus }\n  now: Date\n}): WithdrawOutcome {\n  if (input.current.status !== \"pending\") {\n    throw new Error(\n      `cannot withdraw approval request in status '${input.current.status}'`,\n    )\n  }\n  return { request: { status: \"withdrawn\", decidedAt: input.now } }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/validators/approvals.ts",
  "content": "import { z } from \"zod\"\n\nimport { FUNC_TAXONOMY } from \"~~/shared/taxonomy\"\n\n// SubCat = the l1 leaf inside FUNC_TAXONOMY (e.g. \"systemDesign\",\n// \"softDev\", \"network\", \"embedded\"). Flatten at module load so the\n// validator runs O(1) without re-traversing the constant on each call.\nconst SUB_CAT_KEYS = new Set<string>(\n  FUNC_TAXONOMY.flatMap((c) => c.l1.map((s) => s.key)),\n)\n\nexport const SUB_CAT_KEY_LIST: readonly string[] = [\n  ...FUNC_TAXONOMY.flatMap((c) => c.l1.map((s) => s.key)),\n]\n\nexport const OfficialTier = z.enum([\"productLine\", \"company\"])\nexport type OfficialTier = z.infer<typeof OfficialTier>\n\nconst SubCatKey = z.string().refine((v) => SUB_CAT_KEYS.has(v), {\n  message: \"must be a key from FUNC_TAXONOMY\",\n})\n\nexport const APPROVAL_REASON_MAX = 500\nexport const APPROVAL_NOTE_MAX = 500\n\nconst optionalText = (max: number) =>\n  z\n    .string()\n    .trim()\n    .max(max)\n    .optional()\n    .transform((v) => (v && v.length > 0 ? v : undefined))\n\nexport const SubmitApprovalSchema = z.object({\n  extensionId: z.string().trim().min(1),\n  requestedTier: OfficialTier,\n  subCat: SubCatKey,\n  reason: optionalText(APPROVAL_REASON_MAX),\n})\nexport type SubmitApprovalInput = z.infer<typeof SubmitApprovalSchema>\n\nexport const DecideApprovalSchema = z.object({\n  requestId: z.string().trim().min(1),\n  decision: z.enum([\"approve\", \"reject\"]),\n  note: optionalText(APPROVAL_NOTE_MAX),\n})\nexport type DecideApprovalInput = z.infer<typeof DecideApprovalSchema>\n\nexport const WithdrawApprovalSchema = z.object({\n  requestId: z.string().trim().min(1),\n})\nexport type WithdrawApprovalInput = z.infer<typeof WithdrawApprovalSchema>\n\nexport const AssignReviewerSchema = z.object({\n  tier: OfficialTier,\n  subCat: SubCatKey,\n  userId: z.string().trim().min(1),\n})\nexport type AssignReviewerInput = z.infer<typeof AssignReviewerSchema>\n\nexport const UnassignReviewerSchema = z.object({\n  id: z.string().trim().min(1),\n})\nexport type UnassignReviewerInput = z.infer<typeof UnassignReviewerSchema>\n\nexport const ListApprovalsQuerySchema = z.object({\n  // \"mine\"  → requests this user submitted as a publisher\n  // \"queue\" → pending requests routed to this user as a reviewer\n  view: z.enum([\"mine\", \"queue\"]).default(\"mine\"),\n})\nexport type ListApprovalsQuery = z.infer<typeof ListApprovalsQuerySchema>\n"
}

1	import type { ExtractTablesWithRelations } from "drizzle-orm"
2	import type { PgDatabase, PgQueryResultHKT } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core"
3	
4	import type * as schema from "~~/shared/db/schema"
5	
6	type Schema = typeof schema
7	
8	// `Transactable` covers any concrete Drizzle Postgres database — both the
9	// production `postgres-js` driver and the PGlite driver used in integration
10	// tests — *and* an open transaction handle (`PgTransaction` extends
11	// `PgDatabase`). Repository functions accept this and never branch on the
12	// driver, so an orchestrator can pass either `useDb()` or a `tx` callback
13	// argument and the same repo code works for both.
14	export type Transactable = PgDatabase<
15	  PgQueryResultHKT,
16	  Schema,
17	  ExtractTablesWithRelations<Schema>
18	>
19

13	// `collections` + `collection_items` table accessor. The install
14	// orchestrator uses these to make sure every install also drops a row into
15	// the user's "Installed" system collection; the user-facing collections
16	// feature reuses the same primitives.
17	
18	export type SystemKind = "installed" | "saved"
19	
20	const SYSTEM_KIND_LABEL: Record<SystemKind, string> = {
21	  installed: "Installed",
22	  saved: "Saved",
23	}
24	
25	export type CollectionErrorCode =
26	  | "not_found"
27	  | "forbidden"
28	  | "system_collection_locked"
29	
30	export class CollectionError extends Error {
31	  readonly code: CollectionErrorCode
32	  constructor(code: CollectionErrorCode) {
33	    super(code)
34	    this.code = code
35	    this.name = "CollectionError"
36	  }

39	// Look up (or create) the per-user system collection of the given kind.
40	// Idempotent: safe to call concurrently — the worst case is two rows of
41	// the same kind for the same user, which the install flow then both
42	// `addItem`s into without breakage. If that race ever shows up in prod,
43	// add a partial unique index on (owner_user_id, system_kind).
44	export async function getOrCreateSystem(
45	  db: Transactable,
46	  userId: string,
47	  kind: SystemKind,
48	): Promise<{ id: string; slug: string }> {
49	  const existing = await db
50	    .select({ id: collections.id, slug: collections.slug })
51	    .from(collections)
52	    .where(
53	      and(
54	        eq(collections.ownerUserId, userId),
55	        eq(collections.systemKind, kind),
56	      ),
57	    )
58	    .limit(1)
59	  if (existing[0]) return existing[0]
60	
61	  const id = crypto.randomUUID()
62	  const slug = await generateUniqueShortcode(db)
63	  await db.insert(collections).values({
64	    id,
65	    slug,
66	    ownerUserId: userId,
67	    name: SYSTEM_KIND_LABEL[kind],
68	    systemKind: kind,
69	  })
70	  return { id, slug }
71	}
72	
73	export async function addItem(

77	): Promise<void> {

80	    .values({ collectionId, extensionId })
81	    .onConflictDoNothing()
82	}

106	  nameZh: collections.nameZh,

109	  systemKind: collections.systemKind,
110	  visibility: collections.visibility,
111	  publishedAt: collections.publishedAt,
112	  createdAt: collections.createdAt,
113	  updatedAt: collections.updatedAt,

116	export async function findById(
117	  db: Transactable,
118	  id: string,

121	    .select(fullSelect)
122	    .from(collections)
123	    .where(eq(collections.id, id))

140	export async function findByIdsForUser(
141	  db: Transactable,
142	  collectionIds: string[],
143	  userId: string,
144	): Promise<string[]> {
145	  // Returns the subset that belongs to the given user — used by the
146	  // for-extension membership query so we never leak another user's
147	  // collection ids back to the client.
148	  if (collectionIds.length === 0) return []
149	  const rows = await db
150	    .select({ id: collections.id })
151	    .from(collections)
152	    .where(
153	      and(
154	        inArray(collections.id, collectionIds),
155	        eq(collections.ownerUserId, userId),
156	      ),
157	    )
158	  return rows.map((r) => r.id)
159	}
