161	export async function create(
162	  db: Transactable,
163	  params: { ownerUserId: string; input: CreateCollectionInput },
164	): Promise<CollectionRow> {
165	  const { ownerUserId, input } = params
166	  const id = crypto.randomUUID()
167	  const slug = await generateUniqueShortcode(db)
168	  const visibility = input.visibility ?? "private"
169	  const now = new Date()
170	  await db.insert(collections).values({
171	    id,
172	    slug,
173	    ownerUserId,
174	    name: input.name,
175	    nameZh: input.nameZh ?? null,
176	    description: input.description ?? null,
177	    descriptionZh: input.descriptionZh ?? null,
178	    visibility,
179	    publishedAt: visibility === "public" ? now : null,
180	    createdAt: now,
181	    updatedAt: now,
182	  })
183	  const created = await findById(db, id)
184	  if (!created) throw new Error("collection insert vanished")
185	  return created
186	}
187	
188	export async function update(
189	  db: Transactable,
190	  params: {
191	    slug: string
192	    ownerUserId: string
193	    input: UpdateCollectionInput
194	  },
195	): Promise<CollectionRow> {
196	  const existing = await findBySlug(db, params.slug)
197	  if (!existing) throw new CollectionError("not_found")
198	  if (existing.ownerUserId !== params.ownerUserId) {
199	    throw new CollectionError("forbidden")
200	  }
201	  if (existing.systemKind !== null) {
202	    throw new CollectionError("system_collection_locked")
203	  }
204	
205	  const patch: Partial<typeof collections.$inferInsert> = { updatedAt: new Date() }
206	  const { input } = params
207	  if (input.name !== undefined) patch.name = input.name
208	  if (input.nameZh !== undefined) patch.nameZh = input.nameZh ?? null
209	  if (input.description !== undefined) {
210	    patch.description = input.description ?? null
211	  }
212	  if (input.descriptionZh !== undefined) {
213	    patch.descriptionZh = input.descriptionZh ?? null
214	  }
215	  if (input.visibility !== undefined) {
216	    patch.visibility = input.visibility
217	    // Stamp publishedAt on the first private→public transition. Don't clear
218	    // it on a flip back; "ever-published" sort order stays stable.
219	    if (input.visibility === "public" && existing.publishedAt === null) {
220	      patch.publishedAt = new Date()
221	    }
222	  }
223	
224	  await db.update(collections).set(patch).where(eq(collections.id, existing.id))
225	  const after = await findById(db, existing.id)
226	  if (!after) throw new Error("collection vanished mid-update")
227	  return after
228	}
229	
230	export async function remove(
231	  db: Transactable,
232	  params: { slug: string; ownerUserId: string },
233	): Promise<void> {
234	  const existing = await findBySlug(db, params.slug)
235	  if (!existing) throw new CollectionError("not_found")
236	  if (existing.ownerUserId !== params.ownerUserId) {
237	    throw new CollectionError("forbidden")
238	  }
239	  if (existing.systemKind !== null) {
240	    throw new CollectionError("system_collection_locked")
241	  }
242	  await db.delete(collections).where(eq(collections.id, existing.id))
243	}
244	
245	export async function addItemBySlug(
246	  db: Transactable,
247	  params: { slug: string; ownerUserId: string; extensionId: string },
248	): Promise<void> {
249	  const existing = await findBySlug(db, params.slug)
250	  if (!existing) throw new CollectionError("not_found")
251	  if (existing.ownerUserId !== params.ownerUserId) {
252	    throw new CollectionError("forbidden")
253	  }
254	  await db
255	    .insert(collectionItems)
256	    .values({ collectionId: existing.id, extensionId: params.extensionId })
257	    .onConflictDoNothing()
258	  await db
259	    .update(collections)
260	    .set({ updatedAt: new Date() })
261	    .where(eq(collections.id, existing.id))
262	}
263	
264	export async function removeItemBySlug(
265	  db: Transactable,
266	  params: { slug: string; ownerUserId: string; extensionId: string },
267	): Promise<void> {
268	  const existing = await findBySlug(db, params.slug)
269	  if (!existing) throw new CollectionError("not_found")
270	  if (existing.ownerUserId !== params.ownerUserId) {
271	    throw new CollectionError("forbidden")
272	  }
273	  await db
274	    .delete(collectionItems)
275	    .where(
276	      and(
277	        eq(collectionItems.collectionId, existing.id),
278	        eq(collectionItems.extensionId, params.extensionId),
279	      ),
280	    )
281	  await db
282	    .update(collections)
283	    .set({ updatedAt: new Date() })
284	    .where(eq(collections.id, existing.id))
285	}

287	// Membership lookup for the save-to-collection popover — returns the ids of
288	// the user's collections that already contain the given extension.
289	export async function membershipForExtension(
290	  db: Transactable,
291	  params: { userId: string; extensionId: string },
292	): Promise<string[]> {
293	  const rows = await db
294	    .select({ id: collections.id })
295	    .from(collectionItems)
296	    .innerJoin(collections, eq(collections.id, collectionItems.collectionId))
297	    .where(
298	      and(
299	        eq(collections.ownerUserId, params.userId),
300	        eq(collectionItems.extensionId, params.extensionId),
301	      ),
302	    )
303	  return rows.map((r) => r.id)
304	}

1	import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
2	import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path"
3	import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url"
4	
5	import { PGlite } from "@electric-sql/pglite"
6	import { pg_trgm } from "@electric-sql/pglite/contrib/pg_trgm"
7	import { drizzle, type PgliteDatabase } from "drizzle-orm/pglite"
8	import { migrate } from "drizzle-orm/pglite/migrator"
9	
10	import * as schema from "~~/shared/db/schema"
11	
12	const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)
13	const __dirname = dirname(__filename)
14	const DRIZZLE_DIR = resolve(__dirname, "../../../drizzle")
15	const FTS_SQL_PATH = resolve(DRIZZLE_DIR, "0002_fts_search_vector.sql")
16	
17	export type TestDb = PgliteDatabase<typeof schema>
18	
19	export interface TestDbHandle {
20	  db: TestDb
21	  cleanup: () => Promise<void>
22	}
23	
24	// Boots an in-memory PGlite, applies every Drizzle-tracked migration, and
25	// then layers the manually-authored FTS SQL on top (that file is not part of
26	// drizzle/meta/_journal.json, so the migrator skips it). Returns a fresh
27	// schema per call — call `cleanup()` from `afterAll` to release the WASM
28	// instance.
29	export async function setupDb(): Promise<TestDbHandle> {
30	  const client = new PGlite({ extensions: { pg_trgm } })
31	  const db = drizzle(client, { schema, casing: "snake_case" })
32	
33	  await migrate(db, { migrationsFolder: DRIZZLE_DIR })
34	
35	  const ftsSql = readFileSync(FTS_SQL_PATH, "utf-8")
36	  await client.exec(ftsSql)
37	
38	  return {
39	    db,
40	    cleanup: async () => {
41	      await client.close()
42	    },
43	  }
44	}
45

Used by the approval orchestrator to\n// drive the publisher submit / reviewer decide / publisher withdraw flow.\n\nexport type ApprovalStatus = \"pending\" | \"approved\" | \"rejected\" | \"withdrawn\"\nexport type OfficialTier = \"productLine\" | \"company\"\n\nexport interface ApprovalRequestRow {\n  id: string\n  extensionId: string\n  requestedTier: OfficialTier\n  subCat: string\n  requestedByUserId: string\n  reason: string | null\n  status: ApprovalStatus\n  decidedByUserId: string | null\n  decidedAt: Date | null\n  reviewerNote: string | null\n  createdAt: Date\n  updatedAt: Date\n}\n\nconst fullSelect = {\n  id: approvalRequests.id,\n  extensionId: approvalRequests.extensionId,\n  requestedTier: approvalRequests.requestedTier,\n  subCat: approvalRequests.subCat,\n  requestedByUserId: approvalRequests.requestedByUserId,\n  reason: approvalRequests.reason,\n  status: approvalRequests.status,\n  decidedByUserId: approvalRequests.decidedByUserId,\n  decidedAt: approvalRequests.decidedAt,\n  reviewerNote: approvalRequests.reviewerNote,\n  createdAt: approvalRequests.createdAt,\n  updatedAt: approvalRequests.updatedAt,\n}\n\nexport interface InsertApprovalRequest {\n  id: string\n  extensionId: string\n  requestedTier: OfficialTier\n  subCat: string\n  requestedByUserId: string\n  reason: string | null\n}\n\nexport async function insertRequest(\n  db: Transactable,\n  row: InsertApprovalRequest,\n): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow> {\n  await db.insert(approvalRequests).values(row)\n  const created = await findById(db, row.id)\n  if (!created) throw new Error(\"approval request insert vanished\")\n  return created\n}\n\nexport async function findById(\n  db: Transactable,\n  id: string,\n): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow | null> {\n  const [row] = await db\n    .select(fullSelect)\n    .from(approvalRequests)\n    .where(eq(approvalRequests.id, id))\n    .limit(1)\n  return row ?? null\n}\n\n// Used by the at-most-one-pending guard in the submit orchestrator.\nexport async function findPendingByExtension(\n  db: Transactable,\n  extensionId: string,\n): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow | null> {\n  const [row] = await db\n    .select(fullSelect)\n    .from(approvalRequests)\n    .where(\n      and(\n        eq(approvalRequests.extensionId, extensionId),\n        eq(approvalRequests.status, \"pending\"),\n      ),\n    )\n    .limit(1)\n  return row ?? null\n}\n\n// Publisher's \"my requests\" view.\nexport async function listForPublisher(\n  db: Transactable,\n  userId: string,\n): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow[]> {\n  return db\n    .select(fullSelect)\n    .from(approvalRequests)\n    .where(eq(approvalRequests.requestedByUserId, userId))\n    .orderBy(desc(approvalRequests.createdAt))\n}\n\n// Reviewer's queue — pending requests in any (tier, subCat) cell that the\n// reviewer is assigned to. Implemented as a single query against the cells\n// the reviewer covers; the orchestrator pre-computes the cell list from\n// `approval_reviewers` to keep this method driver-portable (no LATERAL).\nexport async function listPendingForCells(\n  db: Transactable,\n  cells: Array<{ tier: OfficialTier; subCat: string }>,\n): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow[]> {\n  if (cells.length === 0) return []\n  // Build an OR over (tier=, subCat=) pairs. Postgres collapses these into\n  // a single index scan against idx_approval_status_cell.\n  const cellMatches = cells.map((c) =>\n    and(\n      eq(approvalRequests.requestedTier, c.tier),\n      eq(approvalRequests.subCat, c.subCat),\n    ),\n  )\n  return db\n    .select(fullSelect)\n    .from(approvalRequests)\n    .where(\n      and(\n        eq(approvalRequests.status, \"pending\"),\n        sql`(${sql.join(cellMatches, sql` OR `)})`,\n      ),\n    )\n    .orderBy(desc(approvalRequests.createdAt))\n}\n\nexport interface DecidePatch {\n  status: \"approved\" | \"rejected\"\n  decidedByUserId: string\n  decidedAt: Date\n  reviewerNote: string | null\n}\n\nexport async function applyDecision(\n  db: Transactable,\n  id: string,\n  patch: DecidePatch,\n): Promise<void> {\n  await db\n    .update(approvalRequests)\n    .set({ ...patch, updatedAt: new Date() })\n    .where(eq(approvalRequests.id, id))\n}\n\nexport async function applyWithdraw(\n  db: Transactable,\n  id: string,\n  decidedAt: Date,\n): Promise<void> {\n  await db\n    .update(approvalRequests)\n    .set({ status: \"withdrawn\", decidedAt, updatedAt: new Date() })\n    .where(eq(approvalRequests.id, id))\n}\n\n// Companion mutator for the approve path — stamps `officialTier` on the\n// parent extension. Lives here (rather than in `extensions.ts`) because\n// the approval orchestrator is the only legitimate writer; keeping the\n// call adjacent to the request mutation makes that intent obvious.\nexport async function setExtensionOfficialTier(\n  db: Transactable,\n  extensionId: string,\n  tier: OfficialTier,\n): Promise<void> {\n  await db\n    .update(extensions)\n    .set({ officialTier: tier, updatedAt: new Date() })\n    .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))\n}\n\n// Bulk lookup of `officialTier` for a set of extensions — used by the\n// publisher dashboard to render the per-row badge alongside any pending\n// requests in one round-trip.\nexport async function findTiersForExtensions(\n  db: Transactable,\n  extensionIds: string[],\n): Promise<Map<string, OfficialTier | null>> {\n  if (extensionIds.length === 0) return new Map()\n  const rows = await db\n    .select({ id: extensions.id, officialTier: extensions.officialTier })\n    .from(extensions)\n    .where(inArray(extensions.id, extensionIds))\n  return new Map(rows.map((r) => [r.id, r.officialTier ?? null]))\n}\n\n// Used by guards in `decide.post.ts` — confirms a user is assigned to the\n// cell that the request originated from. Super-admins are handled in the\n// orchestrator (a separate join) so this stays a pure reviewer check.\nexport async function isReviewerForCell(\n  db: Transactable,\n  userId: string,\n  tier: OfficialTier,\n  subCat: string,\n): Promise<boolean> {\n  const [row] = await db\n    .select({ id: approvalReviewers.id })\n    .from(approvalReviewers)\n    .where(\n      and(\n        eq(approvalReviewers.userId, userId),\n        eq(approvalReviewers.tier, tier),\n        eq(approvalReviewers.subCat, subCat),\n      ),\n    )\n    .limit(1)\n  return !!row\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/repositories/reviewers.ts",
  "content": "import { and, asc, eq } from \"drizzle-orm\"\n\nimport {\n  approvalReviewers,\n  memberships,\n  users,\n} from \"~~/shared/db/schema\"\n\nimport type { Transactable } from \"./types\"\n\n// `approval_reviewers` table accessor. Backs the reviewer matrix:\n// (tier × subCat) → list of users assigned to decide on that cell.\n// Also exposes the super-admin lookup used by the admin guards.\n\nexport type OfficialTier = \"productLine\" | \"company\"\n\nexport interface ReviewerRow {\n  id: string\n  tier: OfficialTier\n  subCat: string\n  userId: string\n  userEmail: string\n  userName: string | null\n  createdAt: Date\n}\n\nexport interface InsertReviewerRow {\n  id: string\n  tier: OfficialTier\n  subCat: string\n  userId: string\n}\n\n// Full matrix view, joined with `users` so the matrix UI can render\n// reviewer chips with a recognisable label without an extra round-trip.\nexport async function listMatrix(db: Transactable): Promise<ReviewerRow[]> {\n  return db\n    .select({\n      id: approvalReviewers.id,\n      tier: approvalReviewers.tier,\n      subCat: approvalReviewers.subCat,\n      userId: approvalReviewers.userId,\n      userEmail: users.email,\n      userName: users.name,\n      createdAt: approvalReviewers.createdAt,\n    })\n    .from(approvalReviewers)\n    .innerJoin(users, eq(users.id, approvalReviewers.userId))\n    .orderBy(\n      asc(approvalReviewers.tier),\n      asc(approvalReviewers.subCat),\n      asc(users.email),\n    )\n}\n\n// Cells (tier × subCat) where the given user is assigned. Used by the\n// orchestrator to drive `listPendingForCells` from `approvals.ts`.\nexport async function listCellsForUser(\n  db: Transactable,\n  userId: string,\n): Promise<Array<{ tier: OfficialTier; subCat: string }>> {\n  return db\n    .select({\n      tier: approvalReviewers.tier,\n      subCat: approvalReviewers.subCat,\n    })\n    .from(approvalReviewers)\n    .where(eq(approvalReviewers.userId, userId))\n}\n\n// Per-cell reviewer list — useful for the orchestrator's notification fan-out.\nexport async function findReviewersFor(\n  db: Transactable,\n  tier: OfficialTier,\n  subCat: string,\n): Promise<string[]> {\n  const rows = await db\n    .select({ userId: approvalReviewers.userId })\n    .from(approvalReviewers)\n    .where(\n      and(\n        eq(approvalReviewers.tier, tier),\n        eq(approvalReviewers.subCat, subCat),\n      ),\n    )\n  return rows.map((r) => r.userId)\n}\n\nexport async function insertReviewer(\n  db: Transactable,\n  row: InsertReviewerRow,\n): Promise<void> {\n  await db.insert(approvalReviewers).values(row).onConflictDoNothing({\n    target: [\n      approvalReviewers.tier,\n      approvalReviewers.subCat,\n      approvalReviewers.userId,\n    ],\n  })\n}\n\nexport async function deleteReviewer(\n  db: Transactable,\n  id: string,\n): Promise<void> {\n  await db.delete(approvalReviewers).where(eq(approvalReviewers.id, id))\n}\n\n// Super-admin check. A user is a super-admin if any of their memberships\n// carries the `superAdmin` role. Decoupled from a specific org so seeded\n// super-admins keep their authority even when the default org is renamed.\nexport async function isSuperAdmin(\n  db: Transactable,\n  userId: string,\n): Promise<boolean> {\n  const [row] = await db\n    .select({ id: memberships.id })\n    .from(memberships)\n    .where(\n      and(\n        eq(memberships.userId, userId),\n        eq(memberships.role, \"superAdmin\"),\n      ),\n    )\n    .limit(1)\n  return !!row\n}\n"
}

{
  "command": "git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nfeat(approvals): repositories with pglite integration tests\n\nDrizzle-only layer for the approval workflow, following the project's\nload-bearing rule that `drizzle-orm` is imported only inside\n`server/repositories/`.\n\n`server/repositories/approvals.ts`:\n\n- `insertRequest`, `findById`, `findPendingByExtension` — the read/write\n  surface the submit orchestrator needs. `findPendingByExtension` is the\n  query behind the at-most-one-pending guard.\n- `listForPublisher` for the publisher dashboard view, ordered desc on\n  createdAt so the most recent attempt is on top.\n- `listPendingForCells({ tier, subCat }[])` — reviewer queue. Takes the\n  user's cells precomputed from `approval_reviewers` and emits a single\n  query with an OR-of-equalities; Postgres collapses these into an index\n  scan against `idx_approval_status_cell`.\n- `applyDecision`, `applyWithdraw` — state transitions that match the\n  pure decisions in `shared/approvals/state.ts`.\n- `setExtensionOfficialTier` + `findTiersForExtensions` — the parent\n  extension mutation kept adjacent to the request mutation. The setter\n  lives here (not in `extensions.ts`) because this orchestrator is the\n  only legitimate writer of `extensions.officialTier`.\n- `isReviewerForCell` — guard used by the decide endpoint.\n\n`server/repositories/reviewers.ts`:\n\n- `listMatrix` joined with `users` so the matrix UI renders reviewer\n  chips in one round-trip. Ordered `(tier, subCat, email)` to match the\n  matrix's natural read order.\n- `listCellsForUser`, `findReviewersFor`, `insertReviewer` (with\n  `onConflictDoNothing` on the cell-user unique key), `deleteReviewer`.\n- `isSuperAdmin` checks for a membership row with role='superAdmin'.\n  Decoupled from a specific org so seeded super-admins keep their\n  authority even when the default org is renamed.\n\nThe PGlite suite under `tests/integration/repositories/{approvals,\nreviewers}.test.ts` covers each query path against a real migrated DB:\nthe at-most-one-pending guard, the cell-OR query (one cell, multiple\ncells, no matches, empty input), the role-based super-admin lookup,\nand the unique-on-conflict no-op for reviewer assignment.\nEOF\n)\"",
  "description": "Commit 3: repositories"
}

2	import * as filesRepo from "~~/server/repositories/files"

4	import {

8	} from "~~/shared/extensions/state"

10	import { useDb } from "./db"
11	
12	// Orchestrators over the extensions/versions/files repositories. The
13	// branching ("personal scope auto-publishes; org/enterprise waits for
14	// admin") lives in `shared/extensions/state.ts` as pure decision
15	// functions; this file just loads rows, opens transactions, and applies
16	// the decision via the repos.
17	
18	export type { ScanResult }
19	
20	export class VersionStateError extends Error {
21	  readonly code: "version_not_found"
22	  constructor(code: "version_not_found") {
23	    super(code)
24	    this.code = code
25	    this.name = "VersionStateError"
26	  }
27	}
28	
29	// Move a version from `pending|scanning` → `scanning`. Idempotent for those
30	// two start states so a queue retry doesn't get stuck.
31	export async function submit(versionId: string): Promise<void> {
32	  const db = useDb()
33	  const { updated } = await versionsRepo.updateStatusGuarded(db, versionId, {
34	    from: ["pending", "scanning"],
35	    to: "scanning",
36	  })
37	  if (!updated) throw new VersionStateError("version_not_found")
38	}
39	
40	// Apply the bundle scan outcome via `decideScanOutcome`.
41	export async function recordScanResult(
42	  versionId: string,
43	  fileId: string,
44	  result: ScanResult,
45	): Promise<void> {
46	  const db = useDb()
47	  const version = await versionsRepo.findByIdWithScope(db, versionId)
48	  if (!version || version.status !== "scanning") {
49	    throw new VersionStateError("version_not_found")
50	  }
51	
52	  const decision = decideScanOutcome({
53	    scope: version.scope,
54	    result,
55	    now: new Date(),
56	  })
57	
58	  await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
59	    await filesRepo.updateScanStatus(tx, fileId, decision.file)
60	    await versionsRepo.updateStatus(tx, versionId, decision.version)
61	    if (decision.extension) {
62	      await extensionsRepo.updateVisibility(
63	        tx,
64	        version.extensionId,
65	        decision.extension,
66	      )
67	    }
68	  })
69	}
70	
71	// Admin-driven flip from `ready` → `published`. Stamps `publishedAt` on
72	// both rows with the same `now` via `decidePublishOutcome`.
73	export async function publishVersion(
74	  versionId: string,
75	): Promise<{ extensionId: string }> {
76	  const db = useDb()
77	  const row = await versionsRepo.findById(db, versionId)
78	  if (!row || row.status !== "ready") {
79	    throw new VersionStateError("version_not_found")
80	  }
81	
82	  const decision = decidePublishOutcome(new Date())
83	
84	  await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
85	    await extensionsRepo.updateVisibility(
86	      tx,
87	      row.extensionId,
88	      decision.extension,
89	    )
90	    await versionsRepo.updatePublishedAt(
91	      tx,
92	      versionId,
93	      decision.version.publishedAt,
94	    )
95	  })
96	
97	  return { extensionId: row.extensionId }
98	}

65	  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(raw)) {
66	    if (value === undefined) continue

68	  }

78	}

2	import * as extensionsRepo from "~~/server/repositories/extensions"

7	import { useDb } from "./db"

9	// Orchestrator over the installs/collections/extensions/versions repos. The
10	// "which version to install" decision is still inline here; commit 8
11	// extracts it into the pure `shared/installs/record.ts` decision module.
12	
13	export type ExtensionRef = { id: string } | { slug: string }
14	export type InstallSource = "web" | "cli"
15	export type InstallErrorCode = "extension_not_found" | "no_published_version"
16	
17	export class InstallError extends Error {
18	  readonly code: InstallErrorCode
19	  constructor(code: InstallErrorCode) {
20	    super(code)
21	    this.code = code
22	    this.name = "InstallError"
23	  }
24	}
25	
26	export interface RecordInstallParams {
27	  userId: string
28	  extension: ExtensionRef
29	  source: InstallSource
30	  version?: string | undefined
31	}
32	
33	export interface InstallRecord {
34	  installId: string
35	  isFirstInstall: boolean
36	  version: string
37	}
38	
39	export async function recordInstall(
40	  params: RecordInstallParams,
41	): Promise<InstallRecord> {
42	  const { userId, extension, source } = params
43	  const db = useDb()
44	
45	  // Resolve the extension. `findBySlug` is `onlyPublished: true` by default,
46	  // which would hide drafts — the install flow is only allowed against
47	  // published extensions anyway, so the default is what we want.
48	  const ext =
49	    "id" in extension
50	      ? await extensionsRepo.findById(db, extension.id)
51	      : await extensionsRepo.findBySlug(db, extension.slug)
52	  if (!ext) throw new InstallError("extension_not_found")
53	  const extensionId = ext.id
54	
55	  // Resolve which version to install. The orchestrator only loads the
56	  // candidate list when it's actually needed (`requested` is undefined).
57	  const candidates = params.version
58	    ? []
59	    : await versionsRepo.listLatestReadyForExtension(db, extensionId)
60	  const pick = pickInstallVersion({ requested: params.version, candidates })
61	  if (!pick.ok) throw new InstallError(pick.error)
62	  const version = pick.version
63	
64	  const { id: installedColId } = await collectionsRepo.getOrCreateSystem(
65	    db,
66	    userId,
67	    "installed",
68	  )
69	  const installId = crypto.randomUUID()
70	  const resolvedVersion = version
71	
72	  const isFirstInstall = await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
73	    const prior = await installsRepo.findByUserAndExtension(
74	      tx,
75	      userId,
76	      extensionId,
77	    )
78	    const isFirst = prior === null
79	
80	    await installsRepo.insertInstall(tx, {
81	      id: installId,
82	      userId,
83	      extensionId,
84	      version: resolvedVersion,
85	      source,
86	    })
87	    await collectionsRepo.addItem(tx, installedColId, extensionId)
88	    await extensionsRepo.incrementDownloads(tx, extensionId)
89	
90	    return isFirst
91	  })
92	
93	  return { installId, isFirstInstall, version: resolvedVersion }
94	}

Pure\n// transitions live in `shared/approvals/state.ts`; this file loads rows,\n// opens transactions, fires Inngest events, and maps domain errors to\n// HTTP-shaped codes the endpoints translate.\n\nexport type ApprovalErrorCode =\n  | \"extension_not_found\"\n  | \"not_publisher_owner\"\n  | \"extension_not_published\"\n  | \"request_not_found\"\n  | \"request_not_pending\"\n  | \"duplicate_pending_request\"\n  | \"not_reviewer\"\n  | \"not_requester\"\n\nexport class ApprovalError extends Error {\n  readonly code: ApprovalErrorCode\n  constructor(code: ApprovalErrorCode) {\n    super(code)\n    this.code = code\n    this.name = \"ApprovalError\"\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface SubmitParams {\n  extensionId: string\n  requestedTier: OfficialTier\n  subCat: string\n  userId: string\n  reason: string | undefined\n}\n\nexport async function submitRequest(\n  params: SubmitParams,\n): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow> {\n  const db = useDb()\n\n  const ext = await extensionsRepo.findById(db, params.extensionId)\n  if (!ext) throw new ApprovalError(\"extension_not_found\")\n  if (ext.publisherUserId !== params.userId) {\n    throw new ApprovalError(\"not_publisher_owner\")\n  }\n  if (ext.visibility !== \"published\") {\n    throw new ApprovalError(\"extension_not_published\")\n  }\n\n  const row = await db.transaction(async (tx) => {\n    // Re-check inside the transaction — race window between the visibility\n    // load above and the insert below would otherwise let a duplicate slip\n    // through. PG isolation is `read committed` so the second check still\n    // sees a concurrent insert that already committed.\n    const existing = await approvalsRepo.findPendingByExtension(\n      tx,\n      params.extensionId,\n    )\n    if (existing) throw new ApprovalError(\"duplicate_pending_request\")\n\n    return approvalsRepo.insertRequest(tx, {\n      id: crypto.randomUUID(),\n      extensionId: params.extensionId,\n      requestedTier: params.requestedTier,\n      subCat: params.subCat,\n      requestedByUserId: params.userId,\n      reason: params.reason ?? null,\n    })\n  })\n\n  await inngest.send({\n    name: \"extension/approval.requested\",\n    data: {\n      requestId: row.id,\n      extensionId: row.extensionId,\n      requestedTier: row.requestedTier,\n      subCat: row.subCat,\n      requesterUserId: row.requestedByUserId,\n    },\n  })\n\n  return row\n}\n\nexport interface DecideParams {\n  requestId: string\n  action: ApprovalAction\n  reviewerUserId: string\n}\n\nexport async function decideRequest(\n  params: DecideParams,\n): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow> {\n  const db = useDb()\n\n  const current = await approvalsRepo.findById(db, params.requestId)\n  if (!current) throw new ApprovalError(\"request_not_found\")\n  if (current.status !== \"pending\") {\n    throw new ApprovalError(\"request_not_pending\")\n  }\n\n  // Super-admins can decide on any cell; otherwise the reviewer must be\n  // assigned to (requestedTier, subCat) on this request.\n  const allowed =\n    (await reviewersRepo.isSuperAdmin(db, params.reviewerUserId)) ||\n    (await approvalsRepo.isReviewerForCell(\n      db,\n      params.reviewerUserId,\n      current.requestedTier,\n      current.subCat,\n    ))\n  if (!allowed) throw new ApprovalError(\"not_reviewer\")\n\n  const outcome = decideApprovalOutcome({\n    current: {\n      status: current.status,\n      requestedTier: current.requestedTier,\n    },\n    action: params.action,\n    reviewerUserId: params.reviewerUserId,\n    now: new Date(),\n  })\n\n  await db.transaction(async (tx) => {\n    await approvalsRepo.applyDecision(tx, params.requestId, outcome.request)\n    if (outcome.extension) {\n      await approvalsRepo.setExtensionOfficialTier(\n        tx,\n        current.extensionId,\n        outcome.extension.officialTier,\n      )\n    }\n  })\n\n  const updated = await approvalsRepo.findById(db, params.requestId)\n  if (!updated) throw new Error(\"approval request vanished mid-decide\")\n\n  await inngest.send({\n    name: \"extension/approval.decided\",\n    data: {\n      requestId: updated.id,\n      extensionId: updated.extensionId,\n      decision: outcome.request.status,\n      decidedByUserId: params.reviewerUserId,\n    },\n  })\n\n  return updated\n}\n\nexport interface WithdrawParams {\n  requestId: string\n  userId: string\n}\n\nexport async function withdrawRequest(\n  params: WithdrawParams,\n): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow> {\n  const db = useDb()\n\n  const current = await approvalsRepo.findById(db, params.requestId)\n  if (!current) throw new ApprovalError(\"request_not_found\")\n  if (current.requestedByUserId !== params.userId) {\n    throw new ApprovalError(\"not_requester\")\n  }\n  if (current.status !== \"pending\") {\n    throw new ApprovalError(\"request_not_pending\")\n  }\n\n  const outcome = decideWithdrawOutcome({\n    current: { status: current.status },\n    now: new Date(),\n  })\n  await approvalsRepo.applyWithdraw(\n    useDb(),\n    params.requestId,\n    outcome.request.decidedAt,\n  )\n\n  const updated = await approvalsRepo.findById(db, params.requestId)\n  if (!updated) throw new Error(\"approval request vanished mid-withdraw\")\n  return updated\n}\n\n// Reviewer queue — pending requests in any cell this user covers. Returns\n// an empty array when the user has no cell assignments (and is not a\n// super-admin); super-admins see the whole pending queue.\nexport async function listReviewerQueue(\n  userId: string,\n): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow[]> {\n  const db = useDb()\n  if (await reviewersRepo.isSuperAdmin(db, userId)) {\n    // Treat super-admin as \"assigned to every cell\". Pulled from the\n    // matrix verbatim so an empty matrix still surfaces no rows — better\n    // than a silent firehose.\n    const cells = await reviewersRepo\n      .listMatrix(db)\n      .then((rows) =>\n        Array.from(\n          new Set(rows.map((r) => `${r.tier}:${r.subCat}`)),\n        ).map((k) => {\n          const [tier, subCat] = k.split(\":\") as [OfficialTier, string]\n          return { tier, subCat }\n        }),\n      )\n    return approvalsRepo.listPendingForCells(db, cells)\n  }\n\n  const cells = await reviewersRepo.listCellsForUser(db, userId)\n  return approvalsRepo.listPendingForCells(db, cells)\n}\n\nexport async function listPublisherRequests(\n  userId: string,\n): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow[]> {\n  return approvalsRepo.listForPublisher(useDb(), userId)\n}\n"
}

1	import { z } from "zod"
2	import { inngest } from "../inngest"
3	import { publishVersion, VersionStateError } from "../extensions-state"
4	
5	const eventDataSchema = z.object({ versionId: z.string().min(1) })
6	
7	export const reindexSearch = inngest.createFunction(
8	  {
9	    id: "reindex-search",
10	    triggers: [{ event: "extension/index.requested" }],
11	  },
12	  async ({ event, step }) => {
13	    const parsed = eventDataSchema.safeParse(event.data)
14	    if (!parsed.success) {
15	      console.error("[reindex-search] invalid event payload", parsed.error)
16	      return { ok: false, reason: "invalid_event" }
17	    }
18	    const { versionId } = parsed.data
19	
20	    let extensionId: string
21	    try {
22	      const result = await step.run("publish-version", () => publishVersion(versionId))
23	      extensionId = result.extensionId
24	    } catch (err) {
25	      if (err instanceof VersionStateError) {
26	        return { ok: false, reason: err.code }
27	      }
28	      throw err
29	    }
30	
31	    // Nuxt's data layer caches via useFetch keys, not tags. Cache busting on
32	    // the consuming page happens via re-fetch when the user navigates back.
33	    // No revalidateTag equivalent needed here.
34	
35	    await step.sendEvent("notify-published", {
36	      name: "extension/published",
37	      data: { extensionId, versionId },
38	    })
39	
40	    return { ok: true, extensionId }
41	  },

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/server/utils/jobs/notify-approval.ts",
  "content": "import { z } from \"zod\"\n\nimport { inngest } from \"../inngest\"\n\n// Stub notifier for the approval workflow. v1 emits the events; this\n// function logs them to the Inngest dev UI so the event surface is\n// observable end-to-end without a real notification backend. Email and\n// in-app fan-out are P1.\n\nconst requestedSchema = z.object({\n  requestId: z.string().min(1),\n  extensionId: z.string().min(1),\n  requestedTier: z.enum([\"productLine\", \"company\"]),\n  subCat: z.string().min(1),\n  requesterUserId: z.string().min(1),\n})\n\nexport const notifyApprovalRequested = inngest.createFunction(\n  {\n    id: \"notify-approval-requested\",\n    triggers: [{ event: \"extension/approval.requested\" }],\n  },\n  async ({ event }) => {\n    const parsed = requestedSchema.safeParse(event.data)\n    if (!parsed.success) {\n      console.error(\n        \"[notify-approval-requested] invalid event payload\",\n        parsed.error,\n      )\n      return { ok: false, reason: \"invalid_event\" }\n    }\n    // Real backend goes here. The logged shape is the contract the future\n    // mailer will consume.\n    console.info(\n      \"[approvals] new request\",\n      JSON.stringify({ event: \"requested\", ...parsed.data }),\n    )\n    return { ok: true }\n  },\n)\n\nconst decidedSchema = z.object({\n  requestId: z.string().min(1),\n  extensionId: z.string().min(1),\n  decision: z.enum([\"approved\", \"rejected\"]),\n  decidedByUserId: z.string().min(1),\n})\n\nexport const notifyApprovalDecided = inngest.createFunction(\n  {\n    id: \"notify-approval-decided\",\n    triggers: [{ event: \"extension/approval.decided\" }],\n  },\n  async ({ event }) => {\n    const parsed = decidedSchema.safeParse(event.data)\n    if (!parsed.success) {\n      console.error(\n        \"[notify-approval-decided] invalid event payload\",\n        parsed.error,\n      )\n      return { ok: false, reason: \"invalid_event\" }\n    }\n    console.info(\n      \"[approvals] decision\",\n      JSON.stringify({ event: \"decided\", ...parsed.data }),\n    )\n    return { ok: true }\n  },\n)\n"
}

374	export async function getMyExtensions(userId: string) {
375	  const db = useDb()
376	  const rows = await db
377	    .select({
378	      id: extensions.id,
379	      slug: extensions.slug,
380	      name: extensions.name,
381	      category: extensions.category,
382	      visibility: extensions.visibility,
383	      createdAt: extensions.createdAt,
384	      latestVersionId: extensionVersions.id,
385	      latestVersion: extensionVersions.version,
386	      latestStatus: extensionVersions.status,
387	      latestBundleFileId: extensionVersions.bundleFileId,
388	    })
389	    .from(extensions)
390	    .leftJoin(
391	      extensionVersions,
392	      eq(extensionVersions.extensionId, extensions.id),
393	    )
394	    .where(eq(extensions.publisherUserId, userId))
395	    .orderBy(desc(extensions.createdAt), desc(extensionVersions.createdAt))
396	
397	  const byExtension = new Map<string, (typeof rows)[number]>()
398	  for (const row of rows) {
399	    if (!byExtension.has(row.id)) byExtension.set(row.id, row)
400	  }
401	  return Array.from(byExtension.values())
402	}
403	
404	export async function discardDraft(
405	  userId: string,
406	  extensionId: string,
407	): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string }> {
408	  const db = useDb()
409	  const [row] = await db
410	    .select({
411	      publisherUserId: extensions.publisherUserId,
412	      visibility: extensions.visibility,
413	    })
414	    .from(extensions)
415	    .where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))
416	    .limit(1)
417	
418	  if (!row || row.publisherUserId !== userId) {
419	    return { ok: false, error: "not_found" }
420	  }
421	  if (row.visibility !== "draft") {
422	    return { ok: false, error: "not_discardable" }
423	  }
424	
425	  await db.delete(extensions).where(eq(extensions.id, extensionId))
426	  return { ok: true }
427	}
428

1	import * as collectionsRepo from "~~/server/repositories/collections"
2	import { listForOwner as listCollectionsForOwner } from "~~/server/utils/queries/collections"
3	import {
4	  getActivityForUser,
5	  getDraftsForUser,
6	  getInstalledForUser,
7	  getPublishedForUser,
8	  getSavedForUser,
9	} from "~~/server/utils/queries/profile"
10	import type {
11	  ProfileActivityEvent,
12	  ProfileCollectionRow,
13	  ProfileDraftRow,
14	  ProfileInstalledRow,
15	  ProfilePublishedRow,
16	  ProfileSavedRow,
17	} from "~~/shared/types"
18	
19	export type SectionKey =
20	  | "installed"
21	  | "published"
22	  | "drafts"
23	  | "saved"
24	  | "collections"
25	  | "activity"
26	
27	const KEYS: ReadonlySet<SectionKey> = new Set([
28	  "installed",
29	  "published",
30	  "drafts",
31	  "saved",
32	  "collections",
33	  "activity",
34	])
35	
36	export type SectionResponse =
37	  | { section: "installed"; rows: ProfileInstalledRow[] }
38	  | { section: "published"; rows: ProfilePublishedRow[] }
39	  | { section: "drafts"; rows: ProfileDraftRow[] }
40	  | { section: "saved"; rows: ProfileSavedRow[] }
41	  | { section: "collections"; rows: ProfileCollectionRow[] }
42	  | { section: "activity"; rows: ProfileActivityEvent[] }
43	
44	// Map Date fields to ISO strings so the endpoint's return type matches what
45	// crosses the wire. JSON serialization would convert these anyway, but typing
46	// them as Date and serializing them as string is a footgun that hides
47	// type/runtime drift.
48	export default defineEventHandler(async (event): Promise<SectionResponse> => {
49	  const session = await requireUser(event)
50	  const raw = getQuery(event).section
51	  const section = typeof raw === "string" ? raw : "installed"
52	  if (!KEYS.has(section as SectionKey)) {
53	    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: "unknown_section" })
54	  }
55	
56	  switch (section as SectionKey) {
57	    case "installed": {
58	      const rows = await getInstalledForUser(session.id)
59	      return {
60	        section: "installed",
61	        rows: rows.map((r) => ({ ...r, installedAt: r.installedAt.toISOString() })),
62	      }
63	    }
64	    case "published":
65	      // No Date fields on this row.
66	      return { section: "published", rows: await getPublishedForUser(session.id) }
67	    case "drafts": {
68	      const rows = await getDraftsForUser(session.id)
69	      return {
70	        section: "drafts",
71	        rows: rows.map((r) => ({ ...r, updatedAt: r.updatedAt.toISOString() })),
72	      }
73	    }
74	    case "saved": {
75	      const rows = await getSavedForUser(session.id)
76	      return {
77	        section: "saved",
78	        rows: rows.map((r) => ({ ...r, savedAt: r.savedAt.toISOString() })),
79	      }
80	    }
81	    case "collections": {
82	      // Lazily seed the 'Saved' system row so it always appears in the list.
83	      await collectionsRepo.getOrCreateSystem(useDb(), session.id, "saved")
84	      const rows = await listCollectionsForOwner(session.id)
85	      return {
86	        section: "collections",
87	        rows: rows.map((r) => ({ ...r, updatedAt: r.updatedAt.toISOString() })),
88	      }
89	    }
90	    case "activity": {
91	      const rows = await getActivityForUser(session.id)
92	      return {
93	        section: "activity",
94	        rows: rows.map((r) => ({ ...r, at: r.at.toISOString() }) as ProfileActivityEvent),
95	      }
96	    }
97	  }
98	})
99

}\n}\n</script>\n\n<template>\n  <div>\n    <div\n      v-if=\"rows.length === 0\"\n      class=\"rounded-(--radius-card) border border-dashed border-(--color-border) bg-(--color-card)/40 p-10 feat(approvals): publisher dialog and profile requests view

Publisher side of the workflow is now reachable from the UI. The publish
dashboard surfaces the current tier and any pending request inline; an
"Apply for official" button opens a dialog that picks tier + functional
category (defaulting to the extension's existing subCat) and sends the
request. The profile gains a Requests tab where the publisher tracks
status and can withdraw a still-pending request.

Components:

- `app/components/approvals/RequestOfficialDialog.vue` — radio tier
  picker, FUNC_TAXONOMY-grouped subCat dropdown, optional reason
  textarea, error mapping driven by the orchestrator's HTTP status
  messages (`approvals.errors.<code>` with a generic fallback).
- `app/components/profile/SectionRequests.vue` — list view with a

  neutral pending chip (per accent decision #11), reviewer note when
  present, and a Withdraw action while the request is pending.

Server:

- `getRequestsForUser` query in `server/utils/queries/profile.ts` joins
  approval_requests with extensions for display fields, ordered by
  createdAt desc. Plumbed through `server/api/internal/profile/section.get.ts`
  as the new `?section=requests` view.
- `approvalsRepo.findPendingForExtensions` bulk variant so the publisher
  dashboard hydrates per-row pending status in one round-trip; consumed
  by `server/api/internal/publish/my-extensions.get.ts`.
- `getMyExtensions` now also selects `officialTier` and `subCat` so the
  dashboard can render the tier badge and the dialog can default subCat.

i18n: full EN + ZH coverage under `approvals.*` (tier labels, status
chips, dialog copy, error map, empty state) and a new `extensions.
officialTier.*` namespace (Unofficial / Product-Line Official / Company
Official). The existing `extensions.badges.*` keys are left untouched —
commit 7 swaps over the cards, hero, and detail page.

  "content": "import { eq } from \"drizzle-orm\"\nimport { z } from \"zod\"\n\nimport { users } from \"~~/shared/db/schema\"\n\n// Super-admin user lookup by email — backs the \"add reviewer\" picker in\n// the matrix UI. Returns `null` when the user doesn't exist so the\n// client can show a \"no such user\" hint without a 404 round-trip.\nconst querySchema = z.object({\n  email: z.string().trim().email(),\n})\n\nexport default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {\n  await requireSuperAdmin(event)\n  const query = await getValidatedQuery(event, (raw) => querySchema.parse(raw))\n  const [row] = await useDb()\n    .select({ id: users.id, email: users.email, name: users.name })\n    .from(users)\n    .where(eq(users.email, query.email))\n    .limit(1)\n  return { user: row ?? null }\n})\n"
}

Super-admin only.\n\nMiddleware:\n\n- `app/middleware/require-reviewer.ts` and `require-super-admin.ts`\n  follow the same Better-Auth-cookie + $fetch pattern as the existing\n  `require-auth.ts`, redirecting to / for the not-allowed case and to\n  /sign-in for the unauthenticated case.\n\ni18n: new `admin.approvals.*` and `admin.reviewers.matrix.*` namespaces\nin both en and zh. (Vue I18n parses literal `@` as a linked-message\nsigil, so the email field uses a plain \"Email address\" placeholder\nrather than `person@example.com`.)\nEOF\n)\"",

1	import { z } from "zod";
2	
3	const CATEGORIES = ["skills", "mcp", "slash", "plugins"] as const;
4	const SCOPES = ["personal", "org", "enterprise"] as const;
5	const FUNC_CATS = ["workTask", "business", "tools"] as const;
6	const FILTER_CHIPS = ["all", "trending", "new", "official", "free"] as const;
7	const SORTS = ["downloads", "stars", "recent"] as const;
8	const TAG_MATCHES = ["any", "all"] as const;
9	
10	export const PAGE_SIZE = 24;
11	
12	export const filtersSchema = z.object({
13	  q: z.string().trim().min(1).max(120).optional(),
14	  category: z.enum(CATEGORIES).optional(),
15	  scope: z.enum(SCOPES).optional(),
16	  funcCat: z.enum(FUNC_CATS).optional(),
17	  subCat: z.string().trim().min(1).max(40).optional(),
18	  l2: z.string().trim().min(1).max(40).optional(),
19	  // Department id (dotted-path) or the literal "__all" to disable the filter.
20	  dept: z.string().trim().min(1).max(120).optional(),
21	  // Creator = users.id (the user who published). Schema column is named
22	  // publisherUserId for legacy reasons; we expose it as "creator" everywhere.
23	  creator: z.string().trim().min(1).max(80).optional(),
24	  // Publisher = organizations.id (the owning org).
25	  publisher: z.string().trim().min(1).max(80).optional(),
26	  tags: z.array(z.string().trim().min(1).max(40)).max(16).optional(),
27	  tagMatch: z.enum(TAG_MATCHES).optional(),
28	  filter: z.enum(FILTER_CHIPS).optional(),
29	  sort: z.enum(SORTS).optional(),
30	  page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(1000).optional(),
31	});
32	
33	export type Filters = z.infer<typeof filtersSchema>;
34	
35	/**
36	 * Parse Next.js searchParams into typed Filters. Invalid input is dropped,
37	 * so a malformed URL silently falls back to "no filter" rather than 500ing.
38	 */
39	export function parseFilters(
40	  input: Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>,
41	): Filters {
42	  const tags = input.tags;
43	  const normalized = {
44	    ...input,
45	    tags:
46	      tags === undefined
47	        ? undefined
48	        : Array.isArray(tags)
49	          ? tags
50	          : tags.split(",").filter(Boolean),
51	  };
52	  const parsed = filtersSchema.safeParse(normalized);
53	  return parsed.success ? parsed.data : {};
54	}
55	
56	export function pageOffset(page: number | undefined) {
57	  return ((page ?? 1) - 1) * PAGE_SIZE;
58	}
59	
60	/**
61	 * Adapter from `URLSearchParams` (the runtime shape) to the `Record` shape
62	 * `parseFilters` consumes. Repeated keys (`?tags=a&tags=b`) accumulate into
63	 * an array; `serializeFilters` always emits comma-joined, but external
64	 * links may use the array form and the validator already handles both.
65	 */
66	export function searchParamsToInput(
67	  searchParams: URLSearchParams,
68	): Record<string, string | string[]> {
69	  const out: Record<string, string | string[]> = {};
70	  for (const [key, value] of searchParams.entries()) {
71	    const prev = out[key];
72	    if (prev === undefined) {
73	      out[key] = value;
74	    } else if (Array.isArray(prev)) {
75	      prev.push(value);
76	    } else {
77	      out[key] = [prev, value];
78	    }
79	  }
80	  return out;
81	}
82	
83	/**
84	 * Inverse of `parseFilters`. Encodes typed filters back into URL search
85	 * params using the same conventions parseFilters consumes — comma-joined
86	 * arrays for `tags`, omitted keys for undefined / empty values.
87	 */
88	export function serializeFilters(filters: Partial<Filters>): URLSearchParams {
89	  const params = new URLSearchParams();
90	  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(filters)) {
91	    if (value === undefined || value === "" || value === null) continue;
92	    if (Array.isArray(value)) {
93	      if (value.length > 0) params.set(key, value.join(","));
94	    } else {
95	      params.set(key, String(value));
96	    }
97	  }
98	  return params;
99	}
100

1	import { and, desc, eq, ilike, inArray, like, or, sql, type SQL, type ExtractTablesWithRelations } from "drizzle-orm"
2	import type { PgDatabase, PgQueryResultHKT } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core"
3	
4	import { MY_DEPT_ID } from "~~/shared/data/departments"
5	import type * as schema from "~~/shared/db/schema"
6	import { extensions, extensionTags } from "~~/shared/db/schema"
7	import type { Filters } from "~~/shared/validators/filters"
8	
9	const ALL_DEPTS = "__all"
10	
11	// Driver-agnostic: matches postgres-js, PGlite, and PgTransaction so the
12	// query builder composes with the repository layer's `Transactable`.
13	type Db = PgDatabase<
14	  PgQueryResultHKT,
15	  typeof schema,
16	  ExtractTablesWithRelations<typeof schema>
17	>
18	
19	export function buildExtensionWhere(
20	  db: Db,
21	  filters: Filters,
22	  fallbackDeptId?: string,
23	): SQL | undefined {
24	  const clauses = [
25	    eq(extensions.visibility, "published"),
26	
27	    filters.category ? eq(extensions.category, filters.category) : undefined,
28	    filters.scope ? eq(extensions.scope, filters.scope) : undefined,
29	    filters.funcCat ? eq(extensions.funcCat, filters.funcCat) : undefined,
30	    filters.subCat ? eq(extensions.subCat, filters.subCat) : undefined,
31	    filters.l2 ? eq(extensions.l2, filters.l2) : undefined,
32	
33	    filters.creator
34	      ? eq(extensions.publisherUserId, filters.creator)
35	      : undefined,
36	    filters.publisher
37	      ? eq(extensions.ownerOrgId, filters.publisher)
38	      : undefined,
39	
40	    (() => {
41	      const dept = filters.dept ?? fallbackDeptId ?? MY_DEPT_ID
42	      if (dept === ALL_DEPTS) return undefined
43	      // NULL deptId means "system-scoped, applies to every dept" — the
44	      // catalog seeder and seed-mcp-landscape both leave it null because
45	      // their entries are cross-org. Without this branch, those rows are
46	      // invisible to anyone whose default filter lands on a real dept.
47	      return or(
48	        eq(extensions.deptId, dept),
49	        like(extensions.deptId, `${dept}.%`),
50	        sql`${extensions.deptId} IS NULL`,
51	      )
52	    })(),
53	
54	    filters.filter === "trending"
55	      ? sql`${extensions.downloadsCount} > 50000`
56	      : undefined,
57	    filters.filter === "new" ? eq(extensions.badge, "new") : undefined,
58	    filters.filter === "official"
59	      ? eq(extensions.badge, "official")
60	      : undefined,
61	    filters.filter === "free"
62	      ? sql`${extensions.licenseSpdx} IS NOT NULL`
63	      : undefined,
64	
65	    filters.q
66	      ? or(
67	          sql`${extensions.searchVector} @@ websearch_to_tsquery('simple', ${filters.q})`,
68	          ilike(extensions.name, `%${filters.q}%`),
69	          ilike(extensions.nameZh, `%${filters.q}%`),
70	        )
71	      : undefined,
72	
73	    filters.tags && filters.tags.length > 0
74	      ? inArray(
75	          extensions.id,
76	          db
77	            .select({ id: extensionTags.extensionId })
78	            .from(extensionTags)
79	            .where(inArray(extensionTags.tagId, filters.tags))
80	            .groupBy(extensionTags.extensionId)
81	            .having(
82	              filters.tagMatch === "all"
83	                ? sql`count(*) = ${filters.tags.length}`
84	                : sql`count(*) >= 1`,
85	            ),
86	        )
87	      : undefined,
88	  ].filter((c): c is SQL => Boolean(c))
89	
90	  return clauses.length > 0 ? and(...clauses) : undefined
91	}
92	
93	export function buildExtensionOrder(sort: Filters["sort"]) {
94	  switch (sort) {
95	    case "stars":
96	      return [desc(extensions.starsAvg), desc(extensions.downloadsCount)]
97	    case "recent":
98	      return [desc(extensions.publishedAt), desc(extensions.createdAt)]
99	    case "downloads":
100	    default:
101	      return [desc(extensions.downloadsCount)]
102	  }
103	}
104

1	import {
2	  parseFilters,
3	  searchParamsToInput,
4	  serializeFilters,
5	  type Filters,
6	} from "~~/shared/validators/filters"
7	
8	export type FilterUpdate = Partial<Filters>
9	
10	export function useFilters() {
11	  const route = useRoute()
12	  const router = useRouter()
13	  const localePath = useLocalePath()
14	
15	  const filters = computed<Filters>(() => {
16	    const params = new URLSearchParams()
17	    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(route.query)) {
18	      if (Array.isArray(v)) {
19	        for (const item of v) if (item !== null) params.append(k, String(item))
20	      } else if (v !== null && v !== undefined) {
21	        params.append(k, String(v))
22	      }
23	    }
24	    return parseFilters(searchParamsToInput(params))
25	  })
26	
27	  function update(partial: FilterUpdate) {
28	    const next: FilterUpdate = { ...filters.value, ...partial }
29	    if (!("page" in partial)) next.page = undefined
30	    const params = serializeFilters(next)
31	    const qs = params.toString()
32	    const path = route.path
33	    router.replace(qs ? `${path}?${qs}` : path)
34	  }
35	
36	  function hrefForFilters(partial: FilterUpdate, basePath = "/extensions") {
37	    const next: FilterUpdate = { ...filters.value, ...partial }
38	    if (!("page" in partial)) next.page = undefined
39	    const params = serializeFilters(next)
40	    const qs = params.toString()
41	    const path = localePath(basePath)
42	    return qs ? `${path}?${qs}` : path
43	  }
44	
45	  return { filters, update, hrefForFilters }
46	}
47

refactor(extensions): consume officialTier across cards, hero, filters

Card, hero, and related-list components now read `officialTier` instead
of `badge`. The `badge` column stays in the schema and in the frozen
`/api/v1` response so the CLI is unaffected — the v1 mappers derive
`badge: "official"` from `officialTier != null` so any newly-approved
extension still appears with the same shape consumers expect. App code
stops writing `badge` entirely; removing the column rides a future v2
contract bump.

Component changes:

- `ExtCard`, `ExtHero`, `ExtRelatedList` switch `badge` props to
  `officialTier` and render `extensions.officialTier.<tier>` labels.
- The detail page (`pages/extensions/[slug].vue`) updates the prop name
  it passes to `ExtHero`.
- Two new CSS classes in `app/assets/css/tailwind.css`:
  `badge-product-line` (outlined ink) and `badge-company` (filled ink).

  Per accent decision #11 these are neutral chips, never accent fills.

Filter rail:

- `OfficialTierPill` joins `ScopePills` on the same single-row pill rail
  (`FilterBar.vue`) — All / Unofficial / Product-Line / Company. Follows
  the quiet-pill styling from `ScopePills`: neutral ink, bold weight on
  active, no tinted fill.
- `shared/validators/filters.ts` adds a `tier` field
  (`unofficial | productLine | company`). The legacy `filter=official`
  chip remains and now maps to `officialTier IS NOT NULL` (any tier);
  the new `tier=` filter picks a specific cell.
- `shared/search/query.ts` adds the matching clauses and updates the
  legacy `filter=official` chip to use `isNotNull(officialTier)` instead
  of `eq(badge, "official")`, so the chip and the new model agree.

Plumbing:

- `extensions` listSelect / detailSelect / relatedSelect now include
  `officialTier`. `ExtensionListItem` gets the new field, and the
  `collections` query mirroring `listSelect` is updated too so a
  collection detail page doesn't lose the badge.
- Both `/api/v1/extensions` mappers derive `badge` from `officialTier`.
  Contract tests in `tests/contract/extensions-{list,detail}.test.ts`
  stay green — the values still fall inside the existing
  `official | popular | new | null` enum.

i18n: new `filters.tier{Label,*}` keys in en + zh.

42	}
43	
44	function flattenDepts(
45	  list: Department[],
46	  depth = 0,
47	  parentId: string | null = null,
48	  out: FlatDept[] = [],
49	): FlatDept[] {
50	  for (const d of list) {
51	    out.push({
52	      id: d.id,
53	      orgId: ORG_ID,
54	      parentId,
55	      name: d.name,
56	      nameZh: d.nameZh,
57	      pathDepth: depth,
58	    })
59	    if (d.children) flattenDepts(d.children, depth + 1, d.id, out)
60	  }
61	  return out
62	}

64	function slugify(name: string): string {

68	    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "")

89	hand-rolling integrations.

91	## Install
92	
93	\`\`\`bash
94	${installCmd}
95	\`\`\`
96	
97	After installing, restart your agent to pick up the new ${kind}.

99	## Compatibility
100	
101	- **Claude** — supported on the latest agent runtimes
102	- **Other agents** — install paths can be customized via \`agentcenter config\`
103	
104	## Tags

`42-47`: _⚡ Quick win_

**API design: DecideApprovalSchema accepts `note` for approve actions, but the domain model ignores it.**

The validator allows `note` for both `approve` and `reject` decisions, but `ApprovalAction` in `shared/approvals/state.ts` only allows `note` for `reject`. The `decideApprovalOutcome` function hardcodes `reviewerNote: null` for approvals (line 56 in state.ts).

This could confuse API consumers who send a note with an approve action, expecting it to be saved.

Consider either:
1. Use Zod discriminated unions to require `note` only for reject:
   ```typescript
   export const DecideApprovalSchema = z.discriminatedUnion("decision", [
     z.object({ requestId: z.string().trim().min(1), decision: z.literal("approve") }),
     z.object({ 
       requestId: z.string().trim().min(1), 
       decision: z.literal("reject"),
       note: optionalText(APPROVAL_NOTE_MAX),
     }),
   ])
   ```
2. Add a comment documenting that notes are ignored for approve actions.

The current design is functional but could be clearer.

> AGENT

CI is green (validate ✓). CodeRabbit posted one review with 11 findings — no human reviewer yet, no review decision recorded. Here's my read:

**Real bugs worth fixing now (4):**

1. **`RequestOfficialDialog.vue:58-66`** — `t(key, fallback)` doesn't fall back. vue-i18n's second `t()` arg is **interpolation values**, not a fallback. The whole `approvals.errors.<code>` fallback path is dead code. Fix: use `te(key)` to check existence first.

2. **`server/utils/approvals.ts:184-188`** — `applyWithdraw(useDb(), …)` opens a fresh connection instead of reusing the `db` variable defined a few lines above. One-character fix.

3. **`applyDecision` / `applyWithdraw` race window** — no optimistic locking. The orchestrator pre-checks `status === 'pending'` outside a transaction, then writes. Two concurrent reviewers could both succeed. Fix: add `AND status = 'pending'` to the UPDATE WHERE clause and throw if 0 rows affected.

4. **`tailwind.css` badge classes drift from comment** — the comment promises "left rule + bold weight" (per decision #11), but I shipped full borders with normal weight. Either fix the CSS or fix the comment to match.

**Quality wins (3):**

5. `insertRequest` does `INSERT then SELECT` — one Drizzle `.returning()` replaces both.
6. `OfficialTier` / `ApprovalStatus` are redefined in 3 places (`shared/approvals/state.ts`, `shared/db/queries-types.ts`, `server/repositories/{approvals,reviewers}.ts`). Single source of truth would help.
7. `DecideApprovalSchema` accepts `note` for approve too, but the orchestrator drops it — discriminated union would make the API contract honest.

**Nitpicks I'd skip (4):**

- "Show a toast on error" × 3 — the app has no toast system yet; introducing one is its own PR.
- Locale-aware `toLocaleString()` — every existing component in the codebase calls it the same way; not regressing anything.
- `SUB_CAT_KEY_LIST` deriving from `SUB_CAT_KEYS` — cosmetic.
- Map-based dedupe in `listReviewerQueue` — the fragility is theoretical (both halves come from typed enums).
- Middleware ordering "defense in depth" — both pages declare `["require-auth", "require-{reviewer,super-admin}"]` so the order is enforced at the consumer.
- `unassign` should report uncovered cells — feature creep.

Want me to land items 1-7 as a follow-up commit on this branch?

137	export async function listPendingForCells(
138	  db: Transactable,
139	  cells: Array<{ tier: OfficialTier; subCat: string }>,
140	): Promise<ApprovalRequestRow[]> {
141	  if (cells.length === 0) return []
142	  // Build an OR over (tier=, subCat=) pairs. Postgres collapses these into
143	  // a single index scan against idx_approval_status_cell.
144	  const cellMatches = cells.map((c) =>
145	    and(
146	      eq(approvalRequests.requestedTier, c.tier),
147	      eq(approvalRequests.subCat, c.subCat),
148	    ),
149	  )
150	  return db
151	    .select(fullSelect)
152	    .from(approvalRequests)
153	    .where(
154	      and(
155	        eq(approvalRequests.status, "pending"),
156	        sql`(${sql.join(cellMatches, sql` OR `)})`,
157	      ),
158	    )
159	    .orderBy(desc(approvalRequests.createdAt))

167	  params: WithdrawParams,
168	): Promise<approvalsRepo.ApprovalRequestRow> {
169	  const db = useDb()
170	
171	  const current = await approvalsRepo.findById(db, params.requestId)
172	  if (!current) throw new ApprovalError("request_not_found")
173	  if (current.requestedByUserId !== params.userId) {
174	    throw new ApprovalError("not_requester")
175	  }
176	  if (current.status !== "pending") {
177	    throw new ApprovalError("request_not_pending")
178	  }
179	
180	  const outcome = decideWithdrawOutcome({
181	    current: { status: current.status },
182	    now: new Date(),
183	  })
184	  await approvalsRepo.applyWithdraw(
185	    useDb(),
186	    params.requestId,
187	    outcome.request.decidedAt,
188	  )
189	
190	  const updated = await approvalsRepo.findById(db, params.requestId)
191	  if (!updated) throw new Error("approval request vanished mid-withdraw")
192	  return updated
193	}

196	// an empty array when the user has no cell assignments (and is not a

{

  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/validators/approvals.ts",
  "old_string": "export const DecideApprovalSchema = z.object({\n  requestId: z.string().trim().min(1),\n  decision: z.enum([\"approve\", \"reject\"]),\n  note: optionalText(APPROVAL_NOTE_MAX),\n})\nexport type DecideApprovalInput = z.infer<typeof DecideApprovalSchema>",
  "new_string": "// Discriminated union: a reviewer note only makes sense on a rejection.\n// The orchestrator drops any note sent with an approve action anyway —\n// making that explicit at the API boundary catches the mistake before\n// it crosses the wire instead of silently after.\nexport const DecideApprovalSchema = z.discriminatedUnion(\"decision\", [\n  z.object({\n    requestId: z.string().trim().min(1),\n    decision: z.literal(\"approve\"),\n  }),\n  z.object({\n    requestId: z.string().trim().min(1),\n    decision: z.literal(\"reject\"),\n    note: optionalText(APPROVAL_NOTE_MAX),\n  }),\n])\nexport type DecideApprovalInput = z.infer<typeof DecideApprovalSchema>"
}

41	async function handleSubmit(e: Event) {
42	  e.preventDefault()
43	  if (!canSubmit.value) return
44	  busy.value = true
45	  error.value = null
46	  try {

62	        : null

69	  }

## Approved Plan:
# Seed: official tiers, pending requests, decided history

## Context

PR #41 ships the approval workflow + seeds the reviewer matrix and a
super-admin. But after `bun run db:seed` the feature is **invisible**:

- All 16 seeded extensions carry `officialTier: null`, so neither the
  new tier badges (in `ExtCard`, `ExtHero`, `ExtRelatedList`) nor the
  `OfficialTierPill` ever has anything to show.
- `/admin/approvals` lands on an empty queue. To get a single row you
  have to open another tab, log in as a publisher, and submit a
  request — friction that makes manual QA and demos awkward.
- The publisher's profile Requests tab has the same "empty until you
  manually create something" problem.

The fix is small and self-contained: stamp a handful of seeded
extensions with `officialTier`, and pre-create a small spread of
`approval_requests` rows in different states so every visible code
path has data on first load.

This is a **demo-data** change, not a test-coverage change. The
orchestrator unit tests, PGlite integration tests, and Playwright
specs landed in PR #41 are still the source of truth for correctness;
this plan only makes the feature feel "alive" on a fresh dev DB.

## Approach

### 1. Stamp 5 extensions with `officialTier`

The seed data in `shared/data/extensions.ts:5-310` has 5 entries
flagged `badge: "official"` today. Those are the natural promotion
candidates — they already read as "trusted" in the legacy model.
Split them 3 / 2 across the two tiers so both badge CSS classes
(`badge-product-line` outlined, `badge-company` filled) and both
sides of the tier filter have visible coverage:

| id | name         | subCat (existing) | tier        |
|----|--------------|-------------------|-------------|
| 1  | Web Search Pro | docs            | productLine |
| 3  | GitHub MCP   | vcs               | productLine |
| 6  | Image Vision | docs              | company     |
| 11 | Postgres MCP | data              | company     |
| 14 | K8s MCP      | cloud             | productLine |

**Schema thread**: `Extension` in `shared/types.ts:32-50` doesn't
carry `officialTier` today. Add `officialTier?: "productLine" |
"company" | null` after the `badge` field. Then `scripts/seed.ts`
already constructs `extRows` from `EXTENSIONS` (around lines 172-195)
— pipe `e.officialTier ?? null` into the insert payload alongside the
existing `badge` line. The DB column already exists from PR #41's
migration `drizzle/0008_large_lizard.sql`.

### 2. Seed a spread of approval requests

New file `shared/data/approval-requests.ts` mirroring the shape of
the existing `shared/data/approval-reviewers.ts:10-36`. Four rows
that cover every state the publisher and reviewer UIs care about:

| ext (slug) | requestedBy | tier        | subCat | status    | reviewerNote |
|------------|-------------|-------------|--------|-----------|--------------|
| code-interpreter (id 2) | ben | productLine | softDev | **pending**  | — |
| linear-mcp (id 9?)      | cory | company    | data    | **pending**  | — |
| (one of amy's published) | amy | productLine | softDev | **approved** | — |
| (one of dao's published) | dao | company    | docs    | **rejected** | "Needs a maintainer contact in the manifest." |

Exact extension slugs settled at seed time by looking at which
creator owns which row (the seed already pairs creators round-robin
via `CREATORS[i % CREATORS.length]`); the data file lists `(creator
email, tier, subCat, status, reviewerNote?)` and the seed script
resolves it by picking the *first* extension owned by that creator
that isn't already carrying an `officialTier`.

**Invariant to honor**: the orchestrator enforces *at most one
pending request per extension*. The seed must not put two pending
rows on the same extension. Pick distinct extensions; the lookup is
trivial since each creator owns 2-3 rows.

### 3. Wire it into `scripts/seed.ts`

Insertion seam: after `extensionTags` insert (around line 274) and
before the collections truncate (around line 282) — at that point
all `extRows` and `membershipRows` exist with stable ids, so the
data file's email/slug references resolve cleanly.

Follow the same "skip missing references with a warning" pattern
the existing reviewer-matrix seed uses (`scripts/seed.ts` warns
instead of failing on unknown emails). Keeps the seed robust if
someone renames a creator.

## Critical files

Modified:
- `shared/types.ts:32-50` — add optional `officialTier` to `Extension`.
- `shared/data/extensions.ts` — set `officialTier` on the 5 rows
  listed in the table above.
- `scripts/seed.ts` — include `officialTier` in the `extRows` insert
  payload; add a new block after `extensionTags` insertion that
  resolves `APPROVAL_REQUESTS` against creator emails + ext rows and
  inserts into `approvalRequests`.

New:
- `shared/data/approval-requests.ts` — the typed list of 4 demo
  rows in the shape above. Mirror the documentation style of
  `shared/data/approval-reviewers.ts`.

Reuse:
- `CREATORS` array in `scripts/seed.ts:26-33` for email→id resolution.
- `extRows` / `usedSlugs` already built in `scripts/seed.ts:127-148`.
- `approvalRequests` schema from `shared/db/schema/approval.ts`.

## Verification

1. `bun run db:seed` — completes without warnings (all referenced
   creator emails resolve, every approval-request row finds a
   matching extension owned by that creator).
2. `bun run dev`, sign in as `amy@agentcenter.dev` (the seeded
   super-admin):
   - `/en/extensions?tier=productLine` — at least 3 cards visible.
   - `/en/extensions?tier=company` — at least 2 cards visible.
   - `/en/extensions/web-search-pro` — Product-Line Official chip
     in the hero.
   - `/en/admin/approvals` — sees both pending rows (super-admins
     see the full queue).
   - `/en/admin/reviewers` — matrix as before.
3. Sign in as `cory@agentcenter.dev` (reviewer for `productLine ×
   network` and `productLine × embedded`, no super-admin):
   - `/en/admin/approvals` — sees only requests in their assigned
     cells (the linear-mcp pending row if its subCat aligns,
     otherwise none).
4. Sign in as the publisher of the historical approved/rejected
   rows:
   - `/en/profile?section=requests` — shows the approved + rejected
     rows with the reviewer note rendered on the rejection.
5. `bun run validate` + `bun run test:integration` still green — no
   new code paths, but the `EXTENSIONS` array shape change should
   not break the contract tests that snapshot extension payloads.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **Seed reset is destructive** — re-running wipes any in-flight
  real activity. Already true for everything seeded today; not a
  regression.
- **Not a test-coverage replacement** — seed is for visibility,
  not validation. Resist the urge to grow the seed every time a
  bug slips through; the orchestrator tests are the place for that.
- The seeded pending requests are routed through plain `db.insert`,
  *not* via `submitRequest`. That means no `extension/approval.
  requested` Inngest event fires during seed. The dev Inngest UI
  will be empty until a real submit lands — flag this in the seed
  script's logs so it isn't mistaken for a bug.

NOTE:\n  // these rows are inserted directly, bypassing `submitRequest`, so no\n  // `extension/approval.requested` Inngest event fires for them — that's\n  // expected on a fresh seed and not a bug in the workflow.\n  const userIdByCreatorEmail = new Map(CREATORS.map((u) => [u.email, u.id]))\n  const extIdBySlug2 = new Map(extRows.map((r) => [r.slug, r.id]))\n  const approvalRequestRows: {\n    id: string\n    extensionId: string\n    requestedTier: \"productLine\" | \"company\"\n    subCat: string\n    requestedByUserId: string\n    reason: string | null\n    status: \"pending\" | \"approved\" | \"rejected\"\n    decidedByUserId: string | null\n    decidedAt: Date | null\n    reviewerNote: string | null\n  }[] = []\n  const officialTierStamps: { extensionId: string; tier: \"productLine\" | \"company\" }[] = []\n  for (const [i, r] of APPROVAL_REQUESTS.entries()) {\n    const extensionId = extIdBySlug2.get(r.extensionSlug)\n    if (!extensionId) {\n      console.warn(\n        `seed: approval request #${i} references unknown extension slug \"${r.extensionSlug}\" — skipping`,\n      )\n      continue\n    }\n    const publisherId = userIdByCreatorEmail.get(r.publisherEmail)\n    if (!publisherId) {\n      console.warn(\n        `seed: approval request #${i} references unknown publisher ${r.publisherEmail} — skipping`,\n      )\n      continue\n    }\n    let decidedByUserId: string | null = null\n    if (r.decidedByEmail) {\n      decidedByUserId = userIdByCreatorEmail.get(r.decidedByEmail) ?? null\n      if (!decidedByUserId) {\n        console.warn(\n          `seed: approval request #${i} references unknown decider ${r.decidedByEmail} — leaving decidedByUserId null`,\n        )\n      }\n    }\n    const isDecided = r.status === \"approved\" || r.status === \"rejected\"\n    approvalRequestRows.push({\n      id: `appr-req-${i}`,\n      extensionId,\n      requestedTier: r.requestedTier,\n      subCat: r.subCat,\n      requestedByUserId: publisherId,\n      reason: r.reason ?? null,\n      status: r.status,\n      decidedByUserId,\n      decidedAt: isDecided ? new Date() : null,\n      reviewerNote: r.reviewerNote ?? null,\n    })\n    if (r.status === \"approved\") {\n      officialTierStamps.push({ extensionId, tier: r.requestedTier })\n    }\n  }\n  if (approvalRequestRows.length > 0) {\n    console.log(`seed: inserting ${approvalRequestRows.length} approval requests`)\n    await db.insert(approvalRequests).values(approvalRequestRows)\n  }\n  for (const stamp of officialTierStamps) {\n    await db\n      .update(extensions)\n      .set({ officialTier: stamp.tier })\n      .where(sql`${extensions.id} = ${stamp.extensionId}`)\n  }\n  if (officialTierStamps.length > 0) {\n    console.log(\n      `seed: stamped officialTier on ${officialTierStamps.length} extensions to match approved requests`,\n    )\n  }\n\n  // Wipe and re-seed editorial public collections so the /collections browse"
}

## Diagnostic Report: `/en/skills` Showing Only 2 Extensions

**1. Skills-category extensions in `shared/data/extensions.ts`:**

Of the 16 seeded extensions, **5 have `category: "skills"`**:

- ID 1: "Web Search Pro", dept: `eng.cloud.infra`
- ID 2: "Code Interpreter", dept: `eng.product.web`
- ID 6: "Image Vision", dept: `eng.ai.applied`
- ID 10: "Data Analyst", dept: `eng.ai.research`
- ID 13: "Arch Reviewer", dept: `eng.cloud.infra`

Lines: /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/data/extensions.ts:1-315

**2. MY_DEPT_ID value:**

`MY_DEPT_ID = "eng.cloud.infra"`

Line: /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/data/departments.ts:59

**3. Browse filtering (dept filter default behavior):**

In `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/shared/search/query.ts:40-52`, the `buildExtensionWhere` function applies dept filtering:

```typescript
const dept = filters.dept ?? fallbackDeptId ?? MY_DEPT_ID
// Result when no ?dept= param: dept = "eng.cloud.infra"

return or(
  eq(extensions.deptId, dept),           // Exact match
  like(extensions.deptId, `${dept}.%`),  // Descendants
  sql`${extensions.deptId} IS NULL`,     // System-scoped (always visible)
)
```

For an **anonymous browser with no `?dept=` query param**:
- `filters.dept` = undefined
- `fallbackDeptId` = undefined (not passed from API layer)
- Result: `dept = "eng.cloud.infra"` (MY_DEPT_ID)
- Extensions with `deptId IS NULL` **are included** via the OR clause.

**4. Page rendering `/en/skills`:**

File: /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/naive/agentcenter-nuxt/app/pages/skills.vue

The page hard-codes `<ExtensionListing category="skills" />` (line 6), which forces `category="skills"` into the fetch query (line 17 of ExtensionListing.vue).

**5. Prediction for anonymous user on `/en/skills`:**

Expected skills to render (matching `category="skills"` AND dept filter):

- ID 1 "Web Search Pro" (dept: `eng.cloud.infra` — exact match) ✓
- ID 2 "Code Interpreter" (dept: `eng.product.web` — no match) ✗
- ID 6 "Image Vision" (dept: `eng.ai.applied` — no match) ✗
- ID 10 "Data Analyst" (dept: `eng.ai.research` — no match) ✗
- ID 13 "Arch Reviewer" (dept: `eng.cloud.infra` — exact match) ✓

**Root cause: Only 2 of 5 skills extensions have `deptId = "eng.cloud.infra"`**. The other three (ID 2, 6, 10) are filtered out because their dept IDs don't match the hardcoded MY_DEPT_ID and aren't descendants of it. None have `deptId IS NULL`, so they're excluded by the OR clause filter.

// Idempotent catalog seed.
//
// Safe to run on every deploy. Mirrors scripts/seed-mcp-landscape.ts in
// strategy: upserts a fixed inventory of extensions (id prefix `cat-`) plus
// the small set of supporting rows it needs (default org, tag vocabulary),
// then prunes any catalog-prefixed rows no longer in the inventory. Real
// user-published extensions (any non-`cat-` id) are never touched.
//
// Wired into the Vercel build via `vercel-build` so a freshly deployed
// environment carries a populated /extensions catalog.

import { and, inArray, notInArray, sql } from "drizzle-orm"
import { drizzle, type PostgresJsDatabase } from "drizzle-orm/postgres-js"
import postgres from "postgres"

import { CATALOG, type CatalogEntry } from "../shared/data/catalog"
import * as schema from "../shared/db/schema"
import {
  extensions,
  extensionTags,
  organizations,
  tags,
} from "../shared/db/schema"
import { TAG_LABELS } from "../shared/tags"

type Db = PostgresJsDatabase<typeof schema>

const SYSTEM_ORG_ID = "default"
const CATALOG_ID_PREFIX = "cat-"
